sentences.zh: 【序】古今御天下者，其政有四：五帝尚仁，體文德也；

translations.literal: [Preface] Those who have ruled All Under Heaven in past and present times have had four kinds of governance: the Five Emperors esteemed benevolence, embodying civil virtue;
translations.idiomatic: [Preface] From antiquity to the present, those who have governed the realm have pursued four kinds of rule: the Five Emperors prized benevolence and embodied the virtues of civil culture;

sentences.zh: 三王仗義，立武功也；

translations.literal: the Three Kings relied on righteousness and established martial achievement;
translations.idiomatic: the Three Kings relied on righteousness to build their martial renown;

sentences.zh: 五霸崇信，取威令也；

translations.literal: the Five Hegemons honored faith and seized authority by command;
translations.idiomatic: the Five Hegemons exalted trustworthiness to impose their authority;

sentences.zh: 七雄任力，重刑名也。

translations.literal: the Seven Powerful States trusted in force and valued penal law and administrative titles.
translations.idiomatic: the Seven Warring States trusted brute force and prized harsh law and bureaucratic power.

sentences.zh: 蓋仁義既廢，然後齊之以威刑；

translations.literal: For when benevolence and righteousness had been abandoned, then they were regulated by awe-inspiring punishments;
translations.idiomatic: Once benevolence and righteousness had been cast aside, rulers turned to awe-inspiring punishments to keep order;

sentences.zh: 威刑既衰，而酷吏為用，於是商鞅、李斯譎詐設矣。

translations.literal: when awe-inspiring punishments had declined, cruel officials were employed, and thereupon the deceitful stratagems of Shang Yang and Li Si were devised.
translations.idiomatic: when those punishments lost their force, cruel officials came to the fore, and the deceitful schemes of Shang Yang and Li Si were set in place.

sentences.zh: 持法任術，尊君卑臣，奮其策而鞭撻宇宙，持危救弊，先王不得已而用之，天下之人謂之苛法。

translations.literal: Upholding law and relying on technique, they honored the ruler and humbled the ministers, exerting their policies to lash and drive the universe; to sustain a perilous age and remedy its ills, the former kings used such measures only because they had no choice, yet the people of the realm called it harsh law.
translations.idiomatic: They upheld the law and relied on political artifice, exalting the ruler and humbling his ministers, wielding their policies like a whip over the world. The ancient kings resorted to such methods only to save a failing state, yet the people called it cruel law.

sentences.zh: 降及兩漢，承其餘烈。

translations.literal: Descending to the two Han dynasties, they inherited the remaining fierceness.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of the two Han dynasties, that fierce legacy still endured.

sentences.zh: 於是前有郅都、張湯之徒持其刻，後有董宣、陽球之屬肆其猛。

translations.literal: Thus in the earlier period Zhi Du, Zhang Tang, and their kind wielded severity, and later Dong Xuan, Yang Qiu, and their sort unleashed fierceness.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier there were men like Zhi Du and Zhang Tang who carried on that harshness; later came Dong Xuan, Yang Qiu, and others who let their brutality run wild.

sentences.zh: 雖然異代，亦克公方，天下之人謂之酷吏，此又鞅、斯之罪人也！

translations.literal: Although they lived in different ages, they were also able to be impartial and upright; the people of the realm called them cruel officials—yet these were again the guilty heirs of Shang Yang and Li Si!
translations.idiomatic: Though they lived in different eras, they too could be sternly impartial, and the realm called them cruel officials—yet they were only the guilty heirs of Shang Yang and Li Si!

sentences.zh: 然而網既密而奸不勝矣。

translations.literal: Yet though the net was already tight, wrongdoing was not overcome.
translations.idiomatic: Yet even when the net grew tight, crime was never fully overcome.

sentences.zh: 夫子曰：「刑罰不中，則人無所措手足。」

translations.literal: The Master said, "When punishments miss the mark, the people have nowhere to set hand or foot."
translations.idiomatic: The Master said, "When punishments miss the mark, the people do not know where to set hand or foot."

sentences.zh: 誠哉，是言也！

translations.literal: How true indeed are these words!
translations.idiomatic: How true indeed that saying is!

sentences.zh: 唐初革前古之敝，務於勝殘，垂衣而理，且七十載，而人不敢欺。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tang the abuses of former ages were reformed; they strove to overcome cruelty, ruled with robes hanging loose, and for some seventy years the people did not dare to deceive.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tang, the court reformed the abuses of earlier ages, strove to overcome cruelty, and ruled with effortless grace; for some seventy years the people did not dare to deceive one another.

sentences.zh: 由是觀之，在彼不在此。

translations.literal: Viewed from this, it lay in that and not in this.
translations.idiomatic: Seen in this light, the key lay elsewhere, not in harsh punishments themselves.

sentences.zh: 逮則天以女主臨朝，大臣未附；

translations.literal: When it came to Zetian ruling the court as a female sovereign, the great ministers had not yet attached themselves;
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu came to rule as a female sovereign, the great ministers had not yet rallied to her;

sentences.zh: 委政獄吏，剪除宗枝。

translations.literal: she entrusted government to prison officials and cut away the branches of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: she entrusted power to prison officials and cut down the branches of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 於是來俊臣、索元禮、萬國俊、周興、丘神勣、侯思止、郭霸、王弘義之屬，紛紛而出。

translations.literal: Thereupon Lai Junchen, Suo Yuanli, Wan Guojun, Zhou Xing, Qiu Shenji, Hou Sizhi, Guo Ba, Wang Hongyi, and their kind came forth in swarms.
translations.idiomatic: Then men like Lai Junchen, Suo Yuanli, Wan Guojun, Zhou Xing, Qiu Shenji, Hou Sizhi, Guo Ba, and Wang Hongyi appeared one after another.

sentences.zh: 然後起告密之刑，制羅織之獄，生人屏息，莫能自固。

translations.literal: Then were raised the punishments of informing in secret and the prisons of fabricated entrapment; the living held their breath and none could secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: Then came secret denunciations and prisons built on fabricated charges; the living held their breath, and no one could feel secure.

sentences.zh: 至於懷忠蹈義，連頸就戮者，不可勝言。

translations.literal: As for those who cherished loyalty and walked in righteousness, who went to execution with necks linked together, they cannot all be told.
translations.idiomatic: As for the loyal and righteous who went to the block in chains, their number is beyond telling.

sentences.zh: 武後因之坐移唐鼎，天網一舉，而卒籠八荒；

translations.literal: Empress Wu thereby sat and shifted the tripod of Tang; when the heavenly net was raised once, she finally enclosed the eight directions;
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu used this to seize the throne of Tang; once the heavenly net was cast, she finally held all the realm within her grasp;

sentences.zh: 酷之為用，斯害也已。

translations.literal: the use of cruelty—this was the harm of it.
translations.idiomatic: yet the harm done by relying on cruelty was already plain.

sentences.zh: 遂使酷吏之黨，橫噬於朝，制公卿之死命，擅王者之威力。

translations.literal: Thus the faction of cruel officials devoured the court at will, controlled the life and death of dukes and ministers, and usurped the august power of kings.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the party of cruel officials preyed at will upon the court, held the lives of dukes and ministers in their hands, and usurped the power of kings.

sentences.zh: 貴從其欲，毒侈其心，天誅發於脣吻，國柄秉於掌握。

translations.literal: The noble followed their desires; poison swelled their hearts; heaven's punishment issued from their lips, and the handle of state was grasped in their palms.
translations.idiomatic: The powerful indulged their whims; malice swelled their hearts; death sentences issued from their lips, and the reins of state lay in their hands.

sentences.zh: 兇慝之士，榮而慕之，身赴鼎鑊，死而無悔。

translations.literal: Fierce and wicked men honored and admired them, threw themselves into the cauldron and boiling pot, and died without regret.
translations.idiomatic: Vicious men admired them and rushed toward the executioner's cauldron without regret.

sentences.zh: 若是者，何哉？

translations.literal: Men like these—why?
translations.idiomatic: Why were there men like these?

sentences.zh: 要時希旨，見利忘義也！

translations.literal: They seized the moment to please the ruler's intent and, seeing profit, forgot righteousness!
translations.idiomatic: They seized the moment to please their superiors and, seeing profit, forgot righteousness!

sentences.zh: 嘗試而論之，今夫國家行斧鉞之誅，設狴牢之禁以防盜者，雖云固矣，而猶逾垣掘冢，揭篋探囊，死者於前，盜者於後，何者？

translations.literal: Let us try to discuss it: today the state carries out executions by axe and halberd and sets up prison barriers to guard against thieves—though it is said to be secure, still men climb walls and dig graves, pry open chests and probe purses; the dead lie in front and thieves come after. Why?
translations.idiomatic: Consider this: the state executes criminals and locks them in prison to guard against theft—yet though the law is said to be firm, men still scale walls, rob graves, break open chests, and pick pockets; corpses lie ahead and thieves follow behind. Why?

sentences.zh: 以其間有欲也！

translations.literal: Because desire lies between!
translations.idiomatic: Because desire still lies between them and their goal!

sentences.zh: 然所徇者不過數金之資耳！

translations.literal: Yet what they pursue is no more than a few pieces of gold!
translations.idiomatic: Yet all they pursue is no more than a few pieces of gold!

sentences.zh: 彼酷吏與時上下，取重人主，無怵惕之憂，坐致尊寵；

translations.literal: Those cruel officials rose and fell with the times, won weight with the ruler, had no fear or caution, and attained honor and favor while seated;
translations.idiomatic: Those cruel officials rose and fell with the times, won favor with the ruler, lived without fear, and gained rank and honor with little effort;

sentences.zh: 杖起卒伍，富擬封君，豈唯數金之利耶？

translations.literal: whipped up from the ranks of common soldiers, their wealth rivaled that of enfeoffed lords—was it only the profit of a few pieces of gold?
translations.idiomatic: raised from the ranks of common soldiers, they grew as rich as enfeoffed lords—was their reward only a few pieces of gold?

sentences.zh: 則盜官者為幸矣！

translations.literal: Then those who stole office were the fortunate ones!
translations.idiomatic: In that case, those who stole office were the fortunate ones!

sentences.zh: 故有國者則必窒凱覦之路，杜僥幸之門，可不務乎！

translations.literal: Therefore one who holds a state must surely block the road of covetous glances and shut the gate of lucky chance—should this not be pursued?
translations.idiomatic: Surely a ruler must block the road of covetous ambition and shut the gate of lucky chance—should he not make this his task?

sentences.zh: 況乎樂觀時變，恣懷陰賊，斯又郅都、董宣之罪人也。

translations.literal: Moreover, to delight in watching the times change and to indulge a heart of hidden wickedness—this again makes them the guilty heirs of Zhi Du and Dong Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: And when they delight in watching the times change and indulge their hidden malice, they become the guilty heirs of Zhi Du and Dong Xuan as well.

sentences.zh: 異哉，又有效於斯者！

translations.literal: Strange indeed—there were again those who had effect in this!
translations.idiomatic: Strange indeed—there were again men who followed this same path!

sentences.zh: 中興四十載而有吉溫、羅希奭之蠹政，又數載而有敬羽、毛若虛之危法。

translations.literal: Forty years into the Restoration came Ji Wen and Luo Xixia's corrupt government; a few years later came Jing Yu and Mao Ruoxu's perilous law.
translations.idiomatic: Forty years into the Restoration came Ji Wen and Luo Xixia's corrupt rule; a few years later came Jing Yu and Mao Ruoxu's dangerous law.

sentences.zh: 朝經四葉，獄訟再起，比周惡黨，剿絕善人。

translations.literal: The court passed through four reigns; lawsuits and prisons rose again; factions of evil banded together and wiped out good men.
translations.idiomatic: Through four reigns lawsuits and prisons rose again; evil factions banded together and wiped out good men.

sentences.zh: 屢撓將措之刑，以傷太和之氣，幸災樂禍，茍售其身，此又來、索之罪人也！

translations.literal: They repeatedly interfered with punishments about to be set aside, harming the breath of supreme harmony; rejoicing in disaster and delighting in misfortune, they sold themselves for a moment's gain—these were again the guilty heirs of Lai and Suo!
translations.idiomatic: They repeatedly overturned punishments about to be set aside, harming the spirit of harmony; they rejoiced in disaster and sold themselves for gain—these were again the guilty heirs of Lai Junchen and Suo Yuanli!

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 天道禍淫，人道惡殺，既為禍始，必以兇終。

translations.literal: Heaven's Way brings disaster upon the licentious; the human way hates killing. Having been the beginning of disaster, they must end in violence.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's Way brings disaster upon the licentious; the human way hates killing. Those who begin in cruelty must end in violence.

sentences.zh: 故自鞅、斯至於毛、敬，蹈其跡者，卒以誅夷，非不幸也。

translations.literal: Therefore from Shang Yang and Li Si down to Mao and Jing, those who followed in their tracks were finally executed and exterminated—not by misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: From Shang Yang and Li Si down to Mao Ruoxu and Jing Yu, all who followed in their footsteps were finally executed and exterminated—and this was no misfortune.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 執愚賈害，任天下之怨；

translations.literal: Clinging to folly and buying harm, they took upon themselves the resentment of All Under Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Clinging to folly and courting harm, they took upon themselves the resentment of the realm;

sentences.zh: 反道辱名，歸天下之惡。

translations.literal: they turned against the Way and disgraced their names, gathering upon themselves the evil of All Under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: they turned against the Way and disgraced their names, gathering the world's hatred upon themselves.

sentences.zh: 或肆諸原野，人得而誅之；

translations.literal: Some were exposed in the open fields, and men were able to execute them;
translations.idiomatic: Some were exposed in the open fields, where men could execute them;

sentences.zh: 或投之魑魅，鬼得而誅之。

translations.literal: some were cast to demons and goblins, and ghosts were able to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: some were cast to demons and ghosts, where even spirits could punish them.

sentences.zh: 天人報應，豈虛也哉！

translations.literal: The retribution of Heaven and man—how could it be empty!
translations.idiomatic: The retribution of Heaven and man—how could it be empty!

sentences.zh: 俾千載之後，聞其名者，曾蛇豕之不若。

translations.literal: So that a thousand years hence, those who hear their names will find them not even the equal of snakes and swine.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand years hence, those who hear their names will find them worse than snakes and swine.

sentences.zh: 悲夫！

translations.literal: How sad!
translations.idiomatic: How sad!

sentences.zh: 昔《春秋》之義，善惡不隱，今為《酷吏傳》，亦所以示懲勸也。

translations.literal: Formerly the principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals was that good and evil were not concealed; now in composing the Biographies of Cruel Officials, this too is to show warning and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals did not conceal good or evil; in writing these Biographies of Cruel Officials, we likewise intend warning and encouragement.

sentences.zh: 語曰：「前事不忘，將來之師。」

translations.literal: A saying runs, "Do not forget past affairs—they are teachers for the future."
translations.idiomatic: As the saying goes, "Do not forget the past—it is the teacher of the future."

sentences.zh: 意在斯乎！

translations.literal: The meaning lies in this, does it not!
translations.idiomatic: Is that not the point here!

sentences.zh: 意在斯乎！

translations.literal: The meaning lies in this, does it not!
translations.idiomatic: Is that not the point!

sentences.zh: 來俊臣，雍州萬年人也。

translations.literal: Lai Junchen—Lai Junchen was a native of Wannian in Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Junchen was a native of Wannian in Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父操，博徒。

translations.literal: His father Cao was a gambler.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cao was a gambler.

sentences.zh: 與鄉人蔡本結友，遂通其妻，因樗蒲贏本錢數十萬，本無以酬，操遂納本妻。

translations.literal: He became friends with a fellow townsman named Cai Ben, then had relations with Ben's wife; through gambling he won several hundred thousand of Ben's cash, and when Ben could not repay, Cao took Ben's wife.
translations.idiomatic: He befriended a townsman named Cai Ben, then seduced Ben's wife; through gambling he won several hundred thousand of Ben's cash, and when Ben could not repay the debt, Cao took Ben's wife for himself.

sentences.zh: 入操門時，先已有娠，而生俊臣。

translations.literal: When she entered Cao's household she was already pregnant, and bore Junchen.
translations.idiomatic: When she entered Cao's household she was already pregnant, and bore Junchen.

sentences.zh: 兇險不事生產，反覆殘害，舉無與比。

translations.literal: Fierce and dangerous, he would not engage in productive work; repeatedly cruel and harmful, there was none to compare with him.
translations.idiomatic: Violent and treacherous, he would not work for a living; his cruelty was unmatched.

sentences.zh: 曾於和州犯奸盜被鞫，遂妄告密。

translations.literal: Once in He Prefecture he committed adultery and theft and was interrogated; thereupon he falsely reported a secret.
translations.idiomatic: Once in He Prefecture he was tried for adultery and theft, then filed a false secret denunciation.

sentences.zh: 召見奏，刺史東平王續杖之一百。

translations.literal: Summoned to audience to report, the prefectural governor the Prince of Dongping, Xu, had him beaten one hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: When he was summoned to report, the prefectural governor, Prince Xu of Dongping, had him beaten one hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 後續天授中被誅，俊臣復告密，召見，奏言前所告密是豫、博州事，枉被續決杖，遂不得申。

translations.literal: Later Xu was executed in the Tianshou era; Junchen again reported a secret, was summoned to audience, and reported that his earlier secret concerned affairs in Yu and Bo Prefectures, that he had been wrongly beaten by Xu, and thus had been unable to make his case.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xu was executed in the Tianshou era; Junchen filed another secret report and, when summoned, said his earlier denunciation concerned Yu and Bo Prefectures, that Xu had wrongly beaten him, and that he had never been able to make his case heard.

sentences.zh: 則天以為忠，累遷侍御史，加朝散大夫。

translations.literal: Zetian considered him loyal and repeatedly promoted him to Attending Censor, adding the title Grand Master of Palace Leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu considered him loyal and promoted him repeatedly to Attending Censor, with the added title Grand Master of Palace Leisure.

sentences.zh: 按制獄，少不會意者，必引之，前後坐族千餘家。

translations.literal: In handling regulated prisons, if anyone slightly failed to please him, he was sure to implicate him; before and after, more than a thousand clans suffered extermination through association.
translations.idiomatic: In handling political prisoners, anyone who slightly displeased him was sure to be implicated; in all, more than a thousand clans were exterminated through association.

sentences.zh: 二年，擢拜左臺御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the second year he was promoted and appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Left Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Left Bureau.

sentences.zh: 朝廷累息，無交言者，道路以目。

translations.literal: The court held its breath repeatedly; none spoke with one another; on the roads people communicated only with their eyes.
translations.idiomatic: The court held its breath; no one dared speak to another; on the roads people communicated only with their eyes.

sentences.zh: 與侍御史侯思止、王弘義、郭霸、李仁敬，司刑評事康暐、衛遂忠等，同惡相濟。

translations.literal: With Attending Censors Hou Sizhi, Wang Hongyi, Guo Ba, and Li Renjing, and Judicial Reviewers Kang Wei and Wei Suizhong and others, he aided one another in evil.
translations.idiomatic: With Attending Censors Hou Sizhi, Wang Hongyi, Guo Ba, and Li Renjing, and Judicial Reviewers Kang Wei and Wei Suizhong and others, he aided one another in evil.

sentences.zh: 招集無賴數百人，令其告事，共為羅織，千里響應。

translations.literal: He recruited several hundred ruffians, ordered them to report affairs, and together fabricated entrapments; for a thousand li the response echoed.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited several hundred ruffians to file reports and together weave fabricated charges; their network echoed for a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 欲誣陷一人，即數處別告，皆是事狀不異，以惑上下。

translations.literal: When he wished to frame someone, he would have several places lodge separate reports, all with identical circumstances of the case, to confuse above and below.
translations.idiomatic: When he wished to frame someone, he had several places lodge separate reports with identical details, to confuse the court.

sentences.zh: 仍皆云：「請付來俊臣推勘，必獲實情。」

translations.literal: They all still said, "Please assign it to Lai Junchen for investigation—he is sure to obtain the true facts."
translations.idiomatic: They all said, "Please assign the case to Lai Junchen for investigation—he is sure to obtain the true facts."

sentences.zh: 則天於是於麗景門別置推事院，俊臣推勘必獲，專令俊臣等按鞫，亦號為新開門。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zetian specially established an investigation office outside Lijing Gate; Junchen's investigations always obtained results, and she exclusively ordered Junchen and his kind to conduct interrogations—it was also called the Newly Opened Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Empress Wu established a special investigation office outside Lijing Gate; Junchen's investigations always "succeeded," and she gave him and his associates exclusive charge of interrogations—it was also called the Newly Opened Gate.

sentences.zh: 但入新開門者，百不全一。

translations.literal: Of those who merely entered the Newly Opened Gate, not one in a hundred came out whole.
translations.idiomatic: Of those who entered the Newly Opened Gate, not one in a hundred came out alive.

sentences.zh: 弘義戲謂麗景門為「例竟門」，言入此門者，例皆竟也。

translations.literal: Hongyi jested in calling Lijing Gate the "Gate of Invariable Ending," saying that those who entered this gate invariably ended.
translations.idiomatic: Hongyi jested in calling Lijing Gate the "Gate of Invariable Ending," saying that those who entered this gate invariably met their end.

sentences.zh: 俊臣與其黨硃南山輩造《告密羅織經》一卷，皆有條貫支節，布置事狀由緒。

translations.literal: Junchen and his faction, Zhu Nanshan and his kind, composed one scroll of the Classic of Secret Reporting and Fabricated Entrapment, all with connecting threads and sections, arranging the circumstances of cases from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: Junchen and his associates, including Zhu Nanshan, composed a scroll called the Classic of Secret Reporting and Fabricated Entrapment, complete with sections and step-by-step instructions for framing cases.

sentences.zh: 俊臣每鞫囚，無問輕重，多以醋灌鼻，禁地牢中，或盛之甕中，以火圜繞炙之，並絕其糧餉，至有抽衣絮以啖之者。

translations.literal: Whenever Junchen interrogated prisoners, regardless of severity he often poured vinegar into their noses, confined them in underground dungeons, or placed them in jars with fire encircling to roast them, and also cut off their provisions—there were even those who pulled out cotton from clothing to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Junchen interrogated prisoners, regardless of the charge he often poured vinegar into their noses, confined them in underground dungeons, or placed them in jars and roasted them with fire, cut off their food—some even pulled cotton from their clothing to eat.

sentences.zh: 又令寢處糞穢，備諸苦毒。

translations.literal: He also made them sleep amid filth and dung, providing every kind of bitter torment.
translations.idiomatic: He made them sleep amid filth and subjected them to every kind of torment.

sentences.zh: 自非身死，終不得出。

translations.literal: Unless they died in body, they could never leave.
translations.idiomatic: Unless they died, they never left.

sentences.zh: 每有赦令，俊臣必先遣獄卒盡殺重囚，然後宣示。

translations.literal: Whenever there was an amnesty edict, Junchen would first send prison guards to kill all serious prisoners completely, and only then proclaim it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever an amnesty was issued, Junchen first had his guards kill all serious prisoners, and only then proclaimed the edict.

sentences.zh: 又以索元禮等作大枷，凡有十號：一曰定百脈，二曰喘不得，三曰突地吼，四曰著即承，五曰失魂膽，六曰實同反，七曰反是實，八曰死豬愁，九曰求即死，十曰求破家。

translations.literal: He also had Suo Yuanli and others make great cangues, ten kinds in all: first, Fixing the Hundred Meridians; second, Cannot Breathe; third, Earth-Shaking Roar; fourth, Put On and Immediately Confess; fifth, Lost Soul and Gall; sixth, The Fact Is Rebellion; seventh, Rebellion Is the Fact; eighth, Dead Pig in Sorrow; ninth, Seek and Immediately Die; tenth, Seek and Destroy the Family.
translations.idiomatic: He also had Suo Yuanli and others make great cangues, ten kinds in all: Fixing the Hundred Meridians, Cannot Breathe, Earth-Shaking Roar, Put On and Immediately Confess, Lost Soul and Gall, The Fact Is Rebellion, Rebellion Is the Fact, Dead Pig in Sorrow, Seek and Immediately Die, and Seek and Destroy the Family.

sentences.zh: 復有鐵籠頭連其枷者，輪轉於地，斯須悶絕矣。

translations.literal: There were also iron cage-heads linked to the cangues; when rolled on the ground, in an instant one suffocated and fainted.
translations.idiomatic: There were also iron cage-heads linked to the cangues; when a prisoner was rolled on the ground, he suffocated in an instant.

sentences.zh: 囚人無貴賤，必先布枷棒於地，召囚前曰：「此是作具。」

translations.literal: Prisoners, noble or base, were first shown cangues and clubs laid on the ground; the prisoner was summoned forward and told, "These are the implements."
translations.idiomatic: Regardless of rank, prisoners were first shown cangues and clubs laid on the ground and told, "These are the implements."

sentences.zh: 見之魂膽飛越，無不自誣矣。

translations.literal: At the sight, soul and gall flew apart; none failed to falsely incriminate themselves.
translations.idiomatic: At the sight their souls fled; none failed to confess falsely.

sentences.zh: 則天重其賞以酬之，故吏競勸為酷矣。

translations.literal: Zetian heavily rewarded them to repay them, so officials competed to urge one another toward cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu richly rewarded them, so officials competed to outdo one another in cruelty.

sentences.zh: 由是告密之徒，紛然道路；

translations.literal: Thus secret informers swarmed the roads;
translations.idiomatic: Thus secret informers swarmed the roads;

sentences.zh: 名流僶俛閱日而已。

translations.literal: noted men merely bowed their heads and counted the days.
translations.idiomatic: noted men merely bowed their heads and waited for the days to pass.

sentences.zh: 朝士多因入朝，默遭掩襲，以至於族，與其家無復音息。

translations.literal: Many court gentlemen, because they entered court, were silently seized in ambush, even to extermination of the clan; with their families there was no further word.
translations.idiomatic: Many court gentlemen were seized on their way to court without warning, even to the extermination of their clans, and their families heard nothing more.

sentences.zh: 故每入朝者，必與其家訣曰：「不知重相見不？」，

translations.literal: Therefore every man who entered court had to bid farewell to his family, saying, "I do not know whether we shall meet again—"
translations.idiomatic: Therefore every man who went to court bid farewell to his family, saying, "I do not know whether we shall meet again—"

sentences.zh: 地官尚書狄仁傑、益州長史任令暉、冬官尚書李遊道、秋官尚書袁智宏、司賓卿崔神基、文昌左丞盧獻等六人，並為其羅告。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Di Renjie, Regional Commander of Yizhou Ren Linghui, Minister of Works Li Youdao, Minister of Justice Yuan Zhihong, Director of Guests Cui Shenji, and Left Assistant Director of the Palace Secretariat Lu Xian—these six men—were all framed by him.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Revenue Di Renjie, Regional Commander of Yizhou Ren Linghui, Minister of Works Li Youdao, Minister of Justice Yuan Zhihong, Director of Guests Cui Shenji, and Left Assistant Director of the Palace Secretariat Lu Xian—all six were framed by him.

sentences.zh: 俊臣既以族人家為功，茍引之承反，乃奏請降敕，一問即承，同首例得減死。

translations.literal: Junchen, having made exterminating clans his achievement, if he could lead someone to confess rebellion, would memorialize requesting an imperial edict: one question and immediate confession—those who confessed first could have death reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Junchen, having made the extermination of clans his achievement, would try to lead prisoners to confess rebellion, then memorialize for an edict: one question and immediate confession—those who confessed first could have their sentence reduced from death.

sentences.zh: 及脅仁傑等反，仁傑嘆曰：「大周革命，萬物惟新，唐朝舊臣，甘從誅戮。

translations.literal: When he coerced Renjie and the others to confess rebellion, Renjie sighed and said, "The Great Zhou has transformed the realm; all things are renewed. An old minister of Tang willingly accepts execution.
translations.idiomatic: When he coerced Renjie and the others to confess rebellion, Renjie sighed and said, "The Great Zhou has transformed the realm; all things are renewed. As an old minister of Tang, I willingly accept execution.

sentences.zh: 反是實。」

translations.literal: Rebellion is the fact."
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion is the fact—mocking the name of one of the cangues."

sentences.zh: 俊臣乃少寬之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Junchen slightly relaxed his treatment.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Junchen slightly relaxed his treatment.

sentences.zh: 其判官王德壽謂仁傑曰：「尚書事已爾，得減死。

translations.literal: His reviewing official Wang Deshou said to Renjie, "Minister, the matter is already thus—you can have death reduced.
translations.idiomatic: His reviewing official Wang Deshou said to Renjie, "Minister, the matter is settled—you can have your sentence reduced from death.

sentences.zh: 德壽今業已受驅策，欲求少階級，憑尚書牽楊執柔，可乎？」

translations.literal: Deshou has now already been driven to act and wishes to gain a small promotion. Might I rely on the Minister to implicate Yang Zhirou—would that be possible?"
translations.idiomatic: I have already been set to work on this case and wish to gain a small promotion. Could you, Minister, implicate Yang Zhirou for me?"

sentences.zh: 仁傑曰：「若之何？」

translations.literal: Renjie said, "How would that be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Renjie said, "How would that be done?"

sentences.zh: 德壽曰：「尚書昔在春官時，執柔任某司員外，引之可也。」

translations.literal: Deshou said, "When the Minister was formerly in the Ministry of Rites, Zhirou served as an outer-section official in a certain bureau—you could implicate him."
translations.idiomatic: Deshou said, "When you were in the Ministry of Rites, Zhirou served as an outer-section official in your bureau—you could implicate him."

sentences.zh: 仁傑曰：「皇天後土，遣狄仁傑行此事！」

translations.literal: Renjie said, "Heaven above and earth below—would they send Di Renjie to do such a thing!"
translations.idiomatic: Renjie cried, "Heaven and earth—would they send Di Renjie to do such a thing!"

sentences.zh: 以頭觸柱，血流被面，德壽懼而止焉。

translations.literal: He struck his head against a pillar until blood covered his face; Deshou, in fear, stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He struck his head against a pillar until blood covered his face; Deshou, frightened, stopped.

sentences.zh: 仁傑既承反，有司但待報行刑，不復嚴備。

translations.literal: Once Renjie had confessed rebellion, the relevant offices merely awaited the report to carry out execution and no longer kept strict guard.
translations.idiomatic: Once Renjie had confessed rebellion, the authorities merely awaited orders to execute him and no longer kept strict guard.

sentences.zh: 仁傑得憑守者求筆硯，拆被頭帛書之，敘冤苦，置於綿衣，遣謂德壽曰：「時方熱，請付家人去其綿。」

translations.literal: Renjie got the guards to procure brush and inkstone, tore cloth from the head of his quilt to write on it, narrated his grievances, placed it in a padded garment, and sent word to Deshou, saying, "It is hot now—please give it to my family to remove the padding."
translations.idiomatic: Renjie persuaded his guards to bring him brush and inkstone, tore a strip from the head of his quilt to write on, set out his grievances, hid the note in a padded garment, and sent word to Deshou: "It is hot now—please give this to my family and have them remove the padding."

sentences.zh: 德壽不復疑矣，家人得衣中書，仁傑子光遠持之稱變，得召見。

translations.literal: Deshou no longer doubted; the family obtained the letter from within the garment, and Renjie's son Guangyuan presented it as a petition of grievance and was granted an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Deshou no longer suspected a trick. The family found the letter hidden in the garment, and Renjie's son Guangyuan submitted it as an urgent petition and was granted an audience.

sentences.zh: 則天覽之愕然，召問俊臣曰：「卿言仁傑等承反，今子弟訟冤，何故也？」

translations.literal: Zetian read it and was startled; she summoned and questioned Junchen, saying, "You said Renjie and the others confessed rebellion—now their sons and younger brothers petition grievances. Why is this?"
translations.idiomatic: Zetian read it and was stunned. She summoned Junchen and asked, "You said Renjie and the others had confessed rebellion—yet now their sons and brothers are petitioning for justice. How can this be?"

sentences.zh: 俊臣曰：「此等何能自伏其罪！

translations.literal: Junchen said, "How could men like these confess their crimes on their own!
translations.idiomatic: Junchen said, "How could men like these ever confess their crimes on their own!

sentences.zh: 臣寢處甚安，亦不去其巾帶。」

translations.literal: My bedding and quarters are very comfortable, and they still do not remove their caps and sashes."
translations.idiomatic: Their bedding and quarters are quite comfortable, and they still wear their caps and sashes."

sentences.zh: 則天令通事舍人周綝視之。

translations.literal: Zetian ordered the Master of Communications Zhou Can to go inspect.
translations.idiomatic: Zetian ordered the Master of Communications Zhou Can to go and see for himself.

sentences.zh: 俊臣遽令獄卒令假仁傑等巾帶，行立於西，命綝視之。

translations.literal: Junchen hastily ordered prison guards to put caps and sashes on Renjie and the others and have them walk and stand in the west; he ordered Can to inspect.
translations.idiomatic: Junchen hastily had his guards fit Renjie and the others with caps and sashes, make them walk and stand in the west court, and ordered Can to inspect them.

sentences.zh: 綝懼俊臣，莫敢西顧，但視東唯諾而已。

translations.literal: Can feared Junchen and dared not look to the west; he only looked east and assented.
translations.idiomatic: Can feared Junchen and dared not look west; he only glanced east and murmured his assent.

sentences.zh: 俊臣令綝少留，附進狀，乃令判官妄為仁傑等作謝死表，代署而進之。

translations.literal: Junchen had Can stay briefly and attached an advance memorial; then he had his reviewing official falsely compose memorials of thanks for impending death for Renjie and the others, sign on their behalf, and submit them.
translations.idiomatic: Junchen kept Can a little longer and attached a supplemental memorial; then he had his reviewing official forge memorials of thanks for impending death in the names of Renjie and the others, sign them on their behalf, and submit them.

sentences.zh: 鳳閣侍郎樂思晦男年八九歲，其家已族，宜隸於司農，上變，得召見，言「俊臣苛毒，願陛下假條反狀以付之，無大小皆如狀矣。」

translations.literal: Associate Director of the Phoenix Pavilion Le Sihui's son, eight or nine years old—his family had already been exterminated and he was to be enregistered under the Director of Agriculture—presented a petition of grievance, was granted an audience, and said, "Junchen is harsh and poisonous. I wish Your Majesty would lend him a sample indictment of rebellion to put in his hands—then matters great and small would all match the indictment."
translations.idiomatic: Le Sihui's son, Associate Director of the Phoenix Pavilion—eight or nine years old, his clan already exterminated, assigned to the Director of Agriculture—submitted an urgent petition and was granted an audience. He said, "Junchen is cruel beyond measure. Give him a sample indictment of rebellion, and every case, great or small, will match it exactly."

sentences.zh: 則天意少解，乃召見仁傑曰：「卿承反何也？」

translations.literal: Zetian's mind was somewhat relieved; she summoned Renjie and said, "Why did you confess rebellion?"
translations.idiomatic: Zetian's suspicions eased somewhat. She summoned Renjie and asked, "Why did you confess rebellion?"

sentences.zh: 仁傑等曰：「不承反，臣已死於枷棒矣。」

translations.literal: Renjie and the others said, "Had we not confessed rebellion, we would already have died under cangues and clubs."
translations.idiomatic: Renjie and the others said, "Had we not confessed rebellion, we would already have died under the cangues and clubs."

sentences.zh: 則天曰：「何謂作謝死表？」

translations.literal: Zetian said, "What do you mean by writing memorials of thanks for impending death?"
translations.idiomatic: Zetian said, "What do you mean by writing memorials of thanks for impending death?"

sentences.zh: 仁傑曰：「無。」

translations.literal: Renjie said, "There were none."
translations.idiomatic: Renjie said, "We wrote none."

sentences.zh: 因以表示之，乃知其代署，遂出此六家。

translations.literal: Thereupon he presented the memorials, and she then knew they had been signed on their behalf; she thereupon released these six families.
translations.idiomatic: He then produced the memorials, and she saw they had been signed on their behalf. Thereupon she released all six families.

sentences.zh: 俊臣復按大將軍張虔勖、大將軍內侍范雲仙於洛陽牧院。

translations.literal: Junchen again investigated Grand General Zhang Qianxu and Inner Attendant of Grand General Fan Yunxian at the Luoyang Pastoral prison.
translations.idiomatic: Junchen again investigated Grand General Zhang Qianxu and Inner Attendant Fan Yunxian at the Luoyang Pastoral prison.

sentences.zh: 虔勖等不堪其苦，自訟於徐有功，言辭頗厲。

translations.literal: Qianxu and the others could not bear the torment; they complained to Xu Yougong, their words quite fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Qianxu and the others could not endure the torture. They appealed to Xu Yougong, their words sharp and defiant.

sentences.zh: 俊臣命衛士以亂刀斬殺之。

translations.literal: Junchen ordered guards to hack them to death with random blades.
translations.idiomatic: Junchen ordered his guards to hack them to death with random blows.

sentences.zh: 雲仙亦言歷事先朝，稱所司冤苦，俊臣命截去其舌。

translations.literal: Yunxian also spoke of having served the previous dynasty and declared the injustice of his treatment; Junchen ordered his tongue cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Yunxian also spoke of having served the previous dynasty and protested the injustice of his treatment; Junchen ordered his tongue cut out.

sentences.zh: 士庶破膽，無敢言者。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners were terrified; none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners alike were terrified; none dared speak out.

sentences.zh: 俊臣累坐贓，為衛吏紀履忠所告下獄。

translations.literal: Junchen was repeatedly convicted of embezzlement and was denounced and imprisoned by guard officer Ji Lüzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Junchen was repeatedly convicted of embezzlement and was denounced and imprisoned by guard officer Ji Lüzhong.

sentences.zh: 長壽二年，除殿中丞。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changshou, he was appointed Director of the Palace Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Changshou, he was appointed Director of the Palace Directorate.

sentences.zh: 又坐贓，出為同州參軍。

translations.literal: Again convicted of embezzlement, he was sent out as military adjutant of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Again convicted of embezzlement, he was demoted to military adjutant of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 逼奪同列參軍妻，仍辱其母，

translations.literal: He forcibly seized a fellow adjutant's wife and also shamed the man's mother.
translations.idiomatic: He forcibly took a fellow adjutant's wife and humiliated the man's mother as well.

sentences.zh: 萬歲通天元年，召為合宮尉，擢拜洛陽令、司農少卿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wansui Tongtian, He was recalled as Captain of Hegong, then promoted and appointed Magistrate of Luoyang and Vice Director of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wansui Tongtian, He was recalled as Captain of Hegong, then promoted to Magistrate of Luoyang and Vice Director of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 則天賜其奴婢十人，當受於司農。

translations.literal: Zetian bestowed on him ten slave servants; they were to be received from the Director of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Zetian bestowed ten slave servants on him, to be received from the Director of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 時西蕃酋長阿史那斛瑟羅家有細婢，善歌舞，俊臣因令其黨羅告斛瑟羅反，將圖其婢。

translations.literal: At the time the Western Barbarian chieftain Ashina Husheluo had a slender maid skilled in song and dance; Junchen therefore had his followers fabricate a charge that Husheluo was plotting rebellion, intending to seize the maid.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Western tribal chieftain Ashina Husheluo had a slender maid skilled in song and dance. Junchen had his followers fabricate a charge of rebellion against Husheluo, intending to seize the maid.

sentences.zh: 諸蕃長詣闕割耳剺面訟冤者數十人，乃得不族。

translations.literal: Several dozen tribal chiefs came to the palace, cutting their ears and slashing their faces to petition grievances, and only then was the clan not exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen tribal chiefs came to the palace, cutting their ears and slashing their faces to petition for justice—and only then was the clan spared extermination.

sentences.zh: 時綦連耀、劉思禮等有異謀，明堂尉吉頊知之，不自安，以白俊臣發之，連坐族者數十輩。

translations.literal: At the time Qilong Yao, Liu Silim, and others had a separate plot; Bright Hall Captain Ji Tiao knew of it, was ill at ease, and reported to Junchen to expose it; several dozen groups were implicated and their clans exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Qilong Yao, Liu Silim, and others were plotting treason. Bright Hall Captain Ji Tiao knew of it, grew uneasy, and reported it to Junchen to expose the plot. Several dozen groups were implicated and their clans exterminated.

sentences.zh: 俊臣將擅其功，復羅告頊，得召見，僅而免。

translations.literal: Junchen was about to monopolize the credit; he again fabricated charges against Tiao; Tiao was summoned for an audience and narrowly escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Junchen was about to claim all the credit and again fabricated charges against Tiao. Tiao was summoned for an audience and narrowly escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 俊臣先逼妻太原王慶詵女。

translations.literal: Junchen first forced into marriage the daughter of Wang Qingshen of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Junchen had first forced Wang Qingshen's daughter of Taiyuan into marriage.

sentences.zh: 俊臣與河東衛遂忠有舊。

translations.literal: Junchen and Wei Suizhong of Hedong were old acquaintances.
translations.idiomatic: Junchen and Wei Suizhong of Hedong were old acquaintances.

sentences.zh: 遂忠行雖不著，然好學，有詞辯。

translations.literal: Suizhong's conduct was not outstanding, yet he loved learning and had a gift for rhetoric.
translations.idiomatic: Suizhong's conduct was undistinguished, but he loved learning and was skilled in debate.

sentences.zh: 嘗攜酒謁俊臣，俊臣方與妻族宴集，應門者紿云：「已出矣。」

translations.literal: Once he brought wine to visit Junchen; Junchen was just feasting with his wife's kin; the doorkeeper deceived him, saying, "He has already gone out."
translations.idiomatic: Once he brought wine to visit Junchen. Junchen was feasting with his wife's kin, and the doorkeeper lied, saying, "He has already gone out."

sentences.zh: 遂忠知妄，入其宅，慢罵毀辱之。

translations.literal: Suizhong knew it was false, entered his residence, and insulted and reviled him.
translations.idiomatic: Suizhong knew it was a lie, entered the house, and reviled and humiliated him.

sentences.zh: 俊臣恥其妻族，命毆擊反接，既而免之，自此構隙。

translations.literal: Junchen, shamed before his wife's kin, ordered him beaten and bound with hands behind back; afterward he released him—from this arose mutual enmity.
translations.idiomatic: Junchen, shamed before his wife's kin, ordered him beaten and bound with hands behind his back, then released him. From that day they were enemies.

sentences.zh: 俊臣將羅告武氏諸王及太平公主、張易之等，遂相掎摭，則天屢保持之。

translations.literal: Junchen was about to fabricate charges against the princes of the Wu clan, Princess Taiping, Zhang Yizhi, and others; they mutually denounced each other, and Zetian repeatedly protected him.
translations.idiomatic: Junchen was about to fabricate charges against the princes of the Wu clan, Princess Taiping, Zhang Yizhi, and others. They mutually denounced each other, and Zetian repeatedly shielded him.

sentences.zh: 而諸武及太平公主恐懼，共發其罪。

translations.literal: But the Wus and Princess Taiping were fearful and jointly exposed his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: But the Wu princes and Princess Taiping, in fear, jointly exposed his crimes.

sentences.zh: 乃棄市。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: He was executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 國人無少長皆怨之，競剮其肉，斯須盡矣。

translations.literal: People throughout the realm, young and old alike, hated him; they competed to slice his flesh, and in an instant it was gone.
translations.idiomatic: People throughout the realm, young and old alike, hated him. They competed to carve his flesh, and in an instant it was gone.

sentences.zh: 中宗神龍元年三月八日，詔曰：國之大綱，惟刑與政。刑之不中，其政乃虧。劉光業、王德壽、王處貞、屈貞筠、鮑思恭、劉景陽等，庸流賤職，奸吏險夫，以粗暴為能官，以兇殘為奉法。往從按察，害虐在心，倏忽加刑，呼吸就戮，曝骨流血，其數甚多，冤濫之聲，盈於海內。朕唯布新澤，恩被人祇，撫事長懷，尤深惻隱。光業等五人積惡成釁，並謝生涯，雖其人已殂，而其跡可貶，所有官爵，並宜追奪。其枉被殺人，各令州縣以禮埋葬，還其官廕。劉景陽身今見在，情不可矜，特以會恩，免其嚴罰，宜從貶降，以雪冤情，可棣州樂單縣員外尉。自今內外法官，咸宜敬慎。其文深刺骨，跡徇凝脂，高下任情，輕重隨意，如酷吏丘神勣、來子珣、萬國俊、周興、來俊臣、魚承曄、王景昭、索元禮、傅遊藝、王弘義、張知默、裴籍、焦仁亶、侯思止、郭霸、李仁敬、皇甫文備、陳嘉言等，其身已死，自垂拱已來，枉濫殺人，有官者並令削奪。唐奉一依前配流，李秦授、曹仁哲，並與嶺南惡處。

translations.literal: On the eighth day of the third month in the first year of Shenlong under Zhongzong, an edict said: The great framework of the state consists only of punishments and government. If punishments do not hit the mark, government is thereby impaired. Liu Guangye, Wang Deshou, Wang Chuzhen, Qu Zhenyun, Bao Sigong, Liu Jingyang, and the others were common sorts in low offices, treacherous clerks and dangerous men. They treated coarse brutality as capable administration and treated savagery as upholding the law. Formerly, when they followed the inspectors, harm and oppression were in their hearts. In an instant they imposed punishments, and in a breath men went to execution; exposed bones and flowing blood were very numerous. Cries of wrongful and excessive punishment filled the realm. We have only just spread new grace, extending favor to humans and spirits alike. When we consider these affairs, our thoughts are long, and our pity is especially deep. Guangye and the other five men accumulated evil and made crimes; all have already ended their lives. Although the men themselves are dead, their records may still be degraded. All their offices and noble ranks should be stripped posthumously. Those who were wrongfully killed are each to be buried by their prefectures and counties with proper rites, and their official privilege by shadow is to be restored. Liu Jingyang is now still alive, and his circumstances do not deserve pity. Only because he meets this act of grace, he is spared severe punishment. He should be demoted in order to redress the injustice: he may be supernumerary commandant of Ledan County in Dizhou. From now on, legal officials inside and outside the capital should all be reverent and careful. As for those whose written charges cut to the bone, whose traces pursued congealed fat, who made high and low depend on their own feelings and light and heavy depend on their own will, such as the cruel officials Qiu Shenji, Lai Zixun, Wan Guojun, Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, Yu Chengye, Wang Jingzhao, Suo Yuanli, Fu Youyi, Wang Hongyi, Zhang Zhimo, Pei Ji, Jiao Rentan, Hou Sizhi, Guo Ba, Li Renjing, Huangfu Wenbei, Chen Jiayan, and the others: their bodies are already dead, but since the Chuigong era they wrongfully and excessively killed people. Those who held offices are all ordered stripped of them. Tang Fengyi is to remain exiled as before; Li Qinshou and Cao Renzhe are both to be sent to harsh places in Lingnan.

If punishments do not hit the mark, government is thereby impaired. They treated coarse brutality as capable administration and treated savagery as upholding the law. Formerly, when they followed the inspectors, harm and oppression were in their hearts. Those who held offices are all ordered stripped of them. Tang Fengyi is to remain exiled as before; Li Qinshou and Cao Renzhe are both to be sent to harsh places in Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 開元十三年三月十二日，御史大夫程行諶奏：周朝酷吏來子珣、萬國俊、王弘義、侯思止、郭霸、焦仁亶、張知默、李敬仁、唐奉一、來俊臣、周興、丘神勣、索元禮、曹仁哲、王景昭、裴籍、李秦授、劉光業、王德壽、屈貞筠、鮑思恭、劉景陽、王處貞二十三人，殘害宗枝，毒陷良善，情狀尤重，子孫不許與官。陳嘉言、魚承曄、皇甫文備、傅遊藝四人，情狀稍輕，子孫不許近任。周興者，雍州長安人也。

translations.literal: On the twelfth day of the third month in the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan, Censor-in-Chief Cheng Xingchen memorialized: The cruel officials of the Zhou court, Lai Zixun, Wan Guojun, Wang Hongyi, Hou Sizhi, Guo Ba, Jiao Rentan, Zhang Zhimo, Li Jingren, Tang Fengyi, Lai Junchen, Zhou Xing, Qiu Shenji, Suo Yuanli, Cao Renzhe, Wang Jingzhao, Pei Ji, Li Qinshou, Liu Guangye, Wang Deshou, Qu Zhenyun, Bao Sigong, Liu Jingyang, and Wang Chuzhen, twenty-three men, cruelly harmed the imperial clan and maliciously trapped good people. Their circumstances were especially grave, and their descendants should not be allowed to receive office. Chen Jiayan, Yu Chengye, Huangfu Wenbei, and Fu Youyi, four men, had somewhat lighter circumstances, and their descendants should not be allowed to hold posts near the court. Zhou Xing was a man of Chang’an in Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the twelfth day of the third month in the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan, Censor-in-Chief Cheng Xingchen memorialized: The cruel officials of the Zhou court, Lai Zixun, Wan Guojun, Wang Hongyi, Hou Sizhi, Guo Ba, Jiao Rentan, Zhang Zhimo, Li Jingren, Tang Fengyi, Lai Junchen, Zhou Xing, Qiu Shenji, Suo Yuanli, Cao Renzhe, Wang Jingzhao, Pei Ji, Li Qinshou, Liu Guangye, Wang Deshou, Qu Zhenyun, Bao Sigong, Liu Jingyang, and Wang Chuzhen, twenty-three men, cruelly harmed the imperial clan and maliciously trapped good people. Their circumstances were especially grave, and their descendants should not be allowed to receive office. Chen Jiayan, Yu Chengye, Huangfu Wenbei, and Fu Youyi, four men, had somewhat lighter circumstances, and their descendants should not be allowed to hold posts near the court. Zhou Xing was a man of Chang’an in Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 少以明習法律，為尚書省都事。

translations.literal: In youth, through mastery of law, he served as Chief Clerk of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he mastered the law and served as Chief Clerk of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 累遷司刑少卿、秋官侍郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice and Vice Minister of the Autumn Office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice and Vice Minister of the Autumn Office.

sentences.zh: 自垂拱已來，屢受制獄，被其陷害者數千人。

translations.literal: From the Chui Gong era onward, he repeatedly controlled the prison system; those framed by him numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: From the Chui Gong era onward, he repeatedly controlled the prison system, and those he framed numbered in the thousands.

sentences.zh: 天授元年九月革命，除尚書左丞，上疏除李家宗正屬籍。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Tianshou, at the dynastic transformation, he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and memorialized to strike the Li family's imperial clan registry from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the first year of Tianshou, at the dynastic transformation, he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and memorialized to remove the Li family's imperial clan from the registry.

sentences.zh: 二年十一月，與丘神勣同下獄。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year, he was imprisoned together with Qiu Shenji.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the second year, he was imprisoned together with Qiu Shenji.

sentences.zh: 當誅，則天特免之，徙於嶺表。

translations.literal: When he was to be executed, Zetian specially pardoned him and banished him to Lingbiao.
translations.idiomatic: When he was to be executed, Zetian specially pardoned him and banished him to Lingbiao.

sentences.zh: 在道為仇人所殺。

translations.literal: On the road he was killed by an enemy.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he was killed by an enemy.

sentences.zh: 傅遊藝，衛州汲人也。

translations.literal: Fu Youyi—Fu Youyi was a native of Ji in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Youyi was a native of Ji in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 載初元年，為合宮主簿、左肅政臺御史，除左補闕。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zaichu, he served as Registrar of Hegong and Censor of the Left Office of the Imperial Censorate, and was appointed Left Remonstrance Official.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zaichu, he served as Registrar of Hegong and Censor of the Left Office of the Imperial Censorate, and was appointed Left Remonstrance Official.

sentences.zh: 上書稱武氏符瑞，合革姓受命。

translations.literal: He memorialized praising Wu omens and saying the change of surname and receipt of the Mandate were fitting.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized praising Wu omens and declaring that the change of surname and receipt of the Mandate were fitting.

sentences.zh: 則天甚悅，擢為給事中。

translations.literal: Zetian was greatly pleased and promoted him to Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Zetian was greatly pleased and promoted him to Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 數月，加同鳳閣鸞臺平章事。

translations.literal: Within months he was made Associate Director of the Phoenix and Simurgh Pavilions with the same rank as Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Within months he was made Associate Director of the Phoenix and Simurgh Pavilions with the rank of Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 同月，又加朝散大夫，守鸞臺侍郎，依舊同平章事。

translations.literal: In the same month he was further made Grand Master of Palace Attendance and Acting Vice Director of the Simurgh Pavilion, still Associate Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the same month he was further made Grand Master of Palace Attendance and Acting Vice Director of the Simurgh Pavilion, retaining his rank as Associate Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 其年九月革命，改天授元年，賜姓武氏。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year, at the dynastic transformation, the reign was changed to the first year of Tianshou, and he was granted the surname Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of that year, at the dynastic transformation, the reign was changed to the first year of Tianshou, and he was granted the surname Wu.

sentences.zh: 二年五月，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year he was made Silver and Blue Light Chamberlain.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year he was made Silver and Blue Light Chamberlain.

sentences.zh: 兄神童，為冬官尚書，兄弟並承榮寵。

translations.literal: His elder brother Shen Tong served as Minister of Works; the brothers both received glory and favor.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Shen Tong served as Minister of Works; both brothers basked in imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 逾月，除司禮少卿，停知政事。

translations.literal: After more than a month he was appointed Vice Director of Rites and relieved of administrative duties.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a month he was appointed Vice Director of Rites and relieved of his administrative duties.

sentences.zh: 夢登湛露殿，旦而陳於所親，為其所發，伏誅。

translations.literal: He dreamed of ascending the Hall of Clear Dew; at dawn he described it to those close to him; it was reported by them; he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: He dreamed of ascending the Hall of Clear Dew. At dawn he told those close to him, and one of them reported it. He was executed.

sentences.zh: 時人號為四時仕宦，言一年自青而綠，及於硃紫也。

translations.literal: People of the time called it "the four-seasons official career," meaning that within one year one rose from green to purple.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time called it "the four-seasons official career"—meaning that within a single year one rose from green to crimson and purple.

sentences.zh: 希則天旨，誣族皇枝。

translations.literal: He fawned on Zetian's intent and falsely implicated the imperial clan for extermination.
translations.idiomatic: He fawned on Zetian's wishes and falsely implicated members of the imperial clan for extermination.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，禁錮其子孫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, his descendants were confined.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenlong era, his descendants were confined.

sentences.zh: 初，遊藝請則天發六道使，雖身死之後，竟從其謀，於是萬國俊輩恣斬戮矣。

translations.literal: Initially, Youyi asked Zetian to dispatch the Six-Circuit commissioners; though he died afterward, she finally followed his plan, and thereupon Wan Guojun and his kind indulged in slaughter at will.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Youyi asked Zetian to dispatch the Six-Circuit commissioners. Though he died afterward, she eventually adopted his plan, and thereupon Wan Guojun and his kind indulged in slaughter at will.

sentences.zh: 丘神勣，左衛大將軍行恭子也。

translations.literal: Qiu Shenji—Qiu Shenji was the son of Grand General of the Left Guard Xing Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Shenji was the son of Grand General of the Left Guard Xing Gong.

sentences.zh: 永淳元年，為左金吾衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchun, he served as General of the Left Gold Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongchun, he served as General of the Left Gold Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 弘道元年，高宗崩，則天使於巴州害章懷太子，既而歸罪於神勣，左遷疊州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongdao, when Gaozong died, Zetian sent someone to Bazhou to kill Crown Prince Zhanghuai; afterward blame was placed on Shenji and he was demoted to Prefect of Diezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Hongdao, when Gaozong died, Zetian sent someone to Bazhou to kill Crown Prince Zhanghuai. Blame was then placed on Shenji, and he was demoted to Prefect of Diezhou.

sentences.zh: 尋復入為左金吾衛將軍，深見親委。

translations.literal: Soon he returned to office as General of the Left Gold Crow Guard and was deeply trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he returned as General of the Left Gold Crow Guard and was deeply trusted.

sentences.zh: 受詔與周興、來俊臣鞫制獄，俱號為酷吏，

translations.literal: He received orders together with Zhou Xing and Lai Junchen to interrogate fabricated prison cases; all were called cruel officials.
translations.idiomatic: He received orders together with Zhou Xing and Lai Junchen to conduct fabricated prison interrogations; all were called cruel officials.

sentences.zh: 垂拱四年，博州刺史、瑯邪王沖起兵，以神勣為清平道大總管。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chuigong, When Prefect of Bo and Prince of Langye Chong raised troops, Shenji was made Grand Commander of the Qingping Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chuigong, When Prefect of Bo and Prince of Langye Chong raised troops, Shenji was made Grand Commander of the Qingping Circuit.

sentences.zh: 尋而沖為百姓孟青棒、吳希智所殺。

translations.literal: Soon Chong was killed by the commoners Meng Qingbang and Wu Xizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chong was killed by the commoners Meng Qingbang and Wu Xizhi.

sentences.zh: 神勣至州，官吏素服來迎，神勣揮刃盡殺之，破千餘家，因加左金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: When Shenji reached the prefecture, officials in plain dress came to welcome him; Shenji swung his blade and killed them all, destroying more than a thousand households; he was then promoted to Grand General of the Left Gold Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenji reached the prefecture, officials in mourning dress came to welcome him. Shenji swung his blade and killed them all, destroying more than a thousand households. He was then promoted to Grand General of the Left Gold Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 天授二年十月，下詔獄伏誅。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Tianshou, by edict he was imprisoned and executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the second year of Tianshou, by imperial edict he was imprisoned and executed.

sentences.zh: 索元禮，胡人也。

translations.literal: Suo Yuanli—Suo Yuanli was a barbarian.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Yuanli was a barbarian.

sentences.zh: 光宅初，徐敬業起兵揚州，以匡復為名。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangzhai, Xu Jingye raised troops at Yangzhou under the banner of restoration.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Guangzhai era, Xu Jingye raised troops at Yangzhou under the banner of restoration.

sentences.zh: 則天震怒，又恐人心動搖，欲以威制天下。

translations.literal: Zetian was furious and also feared popular unrest; she wished to rule the realm by awe.
translations.idiomatic: Zetian was furious and also feared that hearts would waver; she wished to rule the realm through terror.

sentences.zh: 元禮探其旨，告事。

translations.literal: Yuanli divined her intent and reported cases.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli divined her intent and began reporting cases.

sentences.zh: 召見，擢為遊擊將軍，令於洛州牧院推案制獄。

translations.literal: Summoned for audience, he was promoted to Mobile General and ordered to conduct investigations and fabricated prison cases at the Luoyang Pastoral prison.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned for an audience, he was promoted to Mobile General and ordered to conduct fabricated prison investigations at the Luoyang Pastoral prison.

sentences.zh: 元禮性殘忍，推一人，廣令引數十百人，衣冠震懼，甚於狼虎。

translations.literal: Yuanli was by nature cruel; interrogating one person, he broadly made him implicate dozens or hundreds; officials in caps and gowns trembled in fear more than before wolves and tigers.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli was cruel by nature. Interrogating one person, he would make him implicate dozens or hundreds of others. Officials in caps and gowns trembled before him more than before wolves and tigers.

sentences.zh: 則天數召見賞賜，張其權勢，凡為殺戮者數千人。

translations.literal: Zetian repeatedly summoned and rewarded him, expanding his power; those he killed numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Zetian repeatedly summoned and rewarded him, expanding his power. Those he killed numbered in the thousands.

sentences.zh: 於是周興、來俊臣之徒，效之而起矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, and their kind arose in imitation.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, and their kind arose to imitate him.

sentences.zh: 時有諸州告密人，皆給公乘，州縣護送至闕下，於賓館以廩之。

translations.literal: At the time secret informers from various prefectures were all provided official transport; prefectures and counties escorted them to the capital and lodged them at guest quarters on government rations.
translations.idiomatic: At the time secret informers from various prefectures were all provided official transport; prefectures and counties escorted them to the capital and lodged them at guest quarters on government rations.

sentences.zh: 稍稱旨，必授以爵賞以誘之，貴以威於遠近。

translations.literal: If they slightly pleased her intent, ranks and rewards were invariably granted to entice them, honored to inspire awe in far and near.
translations.idiomatic: If they slightly pleased her, ranks and rewards were invariably granted to entice others, honoring them to inspire awe far and near.

sentences.zh: 元禮尋以酷毒轉甚，則天收人望而殺之。

translations.literal: Before long Yuanli's cruelty grew extreme; Zetian collected popular ill-will and had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yuanli's cruelty grew extreme. Zetian, responding to popular outrage, had him killed.

sentences.zh: 天下之人謂之來、索，言酷毒之極，又首按制獄也。

translations.literal: People throughout the realm called them Lai and Suo, saying their cruelty was the utmost and that they were the first to conduct fabricated prison cases.
translations.idiomatic: People throughout the realm called them "Lai and Suo," saying their cruelty was the utmost and that they were the first to conduct fabricated prison cases.

sentences.zh: 載初元年十月，左臺御史周矩上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Zaichu, Left Office Censor Zhou Ju memorialized in remonstrance, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the first year of Zaichu, Left Office Censor Zhou Ju submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying:

sentences.zh: 頃者小人告訐，習以為常，內外諸司，人懷茍免。

translations.literal: Recently petty men have denounced others, and this has become routine; within and outside the various offices, everyone harbors a wish to escape harm.
translations.idiomatic: Recently petty men have denounced others until it has become routine. Within and outside the various offices, everyone seeks only to escape harm.

sentences.zh: 姑息臺吏，承接強梁，非故欲，規避誣構耳。

translations.literal: Indulging censorial clerks, they consort with the powerful and violent—not because they wish to, but merely to avoid fabricated entrapment.
translations.idiomatic: They indulge censorial clerks and consort with the powerful and violent—not because they wish to, but merely to avoid fabricated entrapment.

sentences.zh: 又推劾之吏，皆以深刻為功，鑿空爭能，相矜以虐。

translations.literal: Also, investigating officers all take harsh severity as achievement; they invent charges out of nothing and compete in ability, each proud of cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating officers all take harsh severity as achievement. They invent charges out of nothing and compete in cruelty, each proud of his brutality.

sentences.zh: 泥耳籠頭，枷研楔轂，折脅簽爪，懸髮薰耳，臥鄰穢溺，曾不聊生，號為「獄持」。

translations.literal: Muddying ears, caging heads, cangues grinding and wedges turning, breaking ribs and piercing fingernails, suspending hair and smoking ears, lying amid neighbors' filth and urine—they have not a moment's peace; these are called "Prison Tortures."
translations.idiomatic: Muddying ears, caging heads, grinding cangues and turning wedges, breaking ribs and piercing fingernails, suspending hair and smoking ears, lying amid neighbors' filth and urine—they have not a moment's peace. These are called "Prison Tortures."

sentences.zh: 或累日節食，連宵緩問，晝夜搖撼，使不得眠，號曰「宿囚」。

translations.literal: Or for days they restrict food, for nights they slow questioning, day and night they shake and jolt them so they cannot sleep; these are called "Overnight Prisoners."
translations.idiomatic: Or for days they restrict food, for nights they prolong questioning, day and night they shake and jolt prisoners so they cannot sleep. These are called "Overnight Prisoners."

sentences.zh: 此等既非木石，且救目前，茍求賒死。

translations.literal: Such men are not wood or stone; to save themselves for the moment, they seek only to postpone death.
translations.idiomatic: Such men are not wood or stone. To save themselves for the moment, they seek only to postpone death.

sentences.zh: 臣竊聽輿議，皆稱天下太平，何苦須反。

translations.literal: I have privately listened to public discussion—all say that under the great peace of the realm, why must one rebel?
translations.idiomatic: I have privately listened to public discussion. All say that under the great peace of the realm, why would anyone rebel?

sentences.zh: 豈被告者盡是英雄，以求帝王耶？

translations.literal: Could all the accused be heroes seeking to become emperors?
translations.idiomatic: Could all the accused be heroes seeking to become emperors?

sentences.zh: 只是不勝楚毒自誣耳。

translations.literal: They simply could not bear the torment and falsely implicated themselves.
translations.idiomatic: They simply could not bear the torture and falsely implicated themselves.

sentences.zh: 何以核之？

translations.literal: How may this be verified?
translations.idiomatic: How may this be verified?

sentences.zh: 陛下試取所告狀酌其虛實者，付令推，微訊動以探其情，所推者必上下其手，希聖旨也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty might try taking denunciation petitions, weighing truth and falsehood, and assigning them for investigation; with slight questioning to probe their feelings, those investigated will invariably manipulate outcomes above and below to match the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty might try taking denunciation petitions, weighing truth and falsehood, and assigning them for investigation. With slight questioning to probe the facts, those conducting the investigation will invariably manipulate the outcome to match what they believe to be Your Majesty's intent.

sentences.zh: 願陛下察之。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to examine this.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to examine this.

sentences.zh: 今滿朝側息不安，皆以為陛下朝與之密，夕與之仇，不可保也。

translations.literal: Now the whole court holds its breath in unease—all believe that whom Your Majesty is intimate with in the morning may be Your Majesty's enemy by evening; none can feel secure.
translations.idiomatic: Now the whole court holds its breath in unease. All believe that whom Your Majesty favors in the morning may be Your Majesty's enemy by evening—no one can feel secure.

sentences.zh: 聞有追攝，與妻子即為死訣。

translations.literal: Hearing that pursuit and seizure are coming, one bids one's wife and children farewell as if for death.
translations.idiomatic: At the mere rumor of arrest, a man bids his wife and children farewell as if for the last time.

sentences.zh: 故為國者以仁為宗，以刑為助。

translations.literal: Therefore one who governs a state takes benevolence as the foundation and punishments as the aid.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever governs a state should make benevolence the foundation and use punishment only as a supplement.

sentences.zh: 周用仁而昌，秦用刑而亡，此之謂也。

translations.literal: Zhou used benevolence and flourished; Qin used punishments and perished—this is what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou prospered through benevolence, while Qin was destroyed through punishment—such is the lesson.

sentences.zh: 願陛下緩刑用仁，天下幸甚！

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to relax punishments and employ benevolence—the realm would be greatly fortunate!
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to ease punishment and govern with benevolence. All under Heaven would rejoice!

sentences.zh: 則天從之，由是制獄稍息。

translations.literal: Wu Zetian followed this; from then on the controlled prisons gradually calmed.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu assented, and thereafter the inquisition prisons grew somewhat quieter.

sentences.zh: 侯思止，雍州醴泉人也。

translations.literal: Hou Sizhi—Hou Sizhi was a native of Liquan in Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Sizhi was a native of Liquan in Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 貧窮不能理生業，乃樂事渤海高元禮家。

translations.literal: Poor and unable to manage a livelihood, he gladly served the household of Gao Yuanli of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Too poor to support himself, he went willingly to work in the household of Gao Yuanli of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 性無賴詭譎。

translations.literal: By nature he was a scoundrel, deceitful and cunning.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was a roguish, deceitful schemer.

sentences.zh: 時恆州刺史裴貞杖一判司。

translations.literal: At that time Pei Zhen, prefect of Hengzhou, caned a judicial aide.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Pei Zhen, the prefect of Hengzhou, had beaten a judicial aide with the staff.

sentences.zh: 則天將不利王室，羅反之徒已興矣。

translations.literal: Wu Zetian was about to harm the royal house; those who framed rebellion were already rising.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu was moving against the imperial clan, and those who fabricated charges of treason were already on the rise.

sentences.zh: 判司教思止說遊擊將軍高元禮，因請狀乃告舒王元名及裴貞反。

translations.literal: The judicial aide taught Sizhi to persuade Mobile General Gao Yuanli; then, requesting a written petition, he denounced Prince Shu Yuanming and Pei Zhen for rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The judicial aide coached Sizhi into persuading Mobile General Gao Yuanli; then, on the pretext of submitting a formal petition, he accused Prince Shu Li Yuanming and Pei Zhen of treason.

sentences.zh: 周興按之，並族滅。

translations.literal: Zhou Xing investigated; all were exterminated, clan and all.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xing investigated the case, and all concerned were executed to the last of their clans.

sentences.zh: 授思止遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: Sizhi was granted the post of Mobile General.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhi was appointed Mobile General.

sentences.zh: 元禮懼而曲媚，引與同坐，呼為侯大，曰：「國家用人以不次，若言侯大不識字，即奏云：『獬豸獸亦不識字，而能觸邪。』」

translations.literal: Yuanli, in fear, fawned obsequiously; he drew him to sit together, called him Lord Hou, and said: "The state employs men out of turn. If one says Lord Hou cannot read characters, then memorialize saying: 'The xiezhi beast also cannot read characters, yet it can touch evil."
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Yuanli flattered him shamelessly. He had him sit beside him, called him "Lord Hou," and said: "The court promotes men by extraordinary appointment. If anyone says Lord Hou is illiterate, memorialize that the xiezhi beast cannot read either, yet it still gores the wicked."

sentences.zh: 則天果如其言，思止以獬豸對之，則天大悅，

translations.literal: Wu Zetian indeed did as he said; Sizhi answered with the xiezhi, and Wu Zetian was greatly pleased.',
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu did exactly as he advised. When questioned, Sizhi answered with the xiezhi comparison, and she was delighted.

sentences.zh: 天授三年，乃拜朝散大夫、左臺侍御史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianshou, he was appointed Grand Master of Palace Leisure and Left Censorate Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianshou, He was then appointed Grand Master of Palace Leisure and Attending Censor of the Left Censorate.

sentences.zh: 元禮復教曰：「在上知侯大無宅，倘以諸役官宅見借，可辭謝而不受。

translations.literal: Yuanli again instructed him, saying: "The sovereign above knows Lord Hou has no house. If various confiscated official residences are offered on loan, you may decline and refuse to accept.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli coached him again: "The Empress knows you have no house. If she offers you one of the confiscated residences of convicted officials, politely refuse.

sentences.zh: 在上必問所由，即奏云：『諸反逆人，臣惡其名，不願坐其宅。』」

translations.literal: The sovereign above will surely ask the reason; then memorialize saying: 'As for all rebel traitors, I hate their names and do not wish to sit in their houses.'"
translations.idiomatic: She is sure to ask why. Then report: 'I detest the names of all traitors and do not wish to dwell in their houses.'"

sentences.zh: 則天復大悅，恩澤甚優。

translations.literal: Wu Zetian again was greatly pleased; his favor and grace were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu was again delighted and showered him with extraordinary favor.

sentences.zh: 思止既按制獄，苛酷日甚。

translations.literal: Once Sizhi undertook investigation of the controlled prisons, severity and cruelty grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sizhi took charge of the inquisition prisons, his cruelty grew worse by the day.

sentences.zh: 嘗按中丞魏元忠，曰：「急認白司馬，不然，即吃孟青。」

translations.literal: Once, interrogating Censor Wei Yuanzhong, he said: "Quickly confess regarding White Horse Slope; otherwise you will taste Meng Qing."
translations.idiomatic: Interrogating Censor-in-Chief Wei Yuanzhong, he said: "Confess at once, or you will taste Meng Qing's club at White Horse Slope."

sentences.zh: 白司馬者，洛陽有阪號白司馬阪。

translations.literal: White Horse Slope"—in Luoyang there is a slope called White Horse Slope.
translations.idiomatic: The name White Horse Slope referred to a slope in Luoyang known by that name.

sentences.zh: 孟青者，將軍姓孟名青棒，即殺瑯邪王沖者也。

translations.literal: "Meng Qing"—a general surnamed Meng named Qingbang, the one who killed Prince of Langye Chong.
translations.idiomatic: "Meng Qing" was a general named Meng Qingbang—the man who had executed Prince Chong of Langye.

sentences.zh: 思止閭巷庸奴，常以此謂諸囚也。

translations.literal: Sizhi, an alleyway drudge, constantly used these phrases toward all prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhi, a nobody from the lanes, constantly used these threats against every prisoner.

sentences.zh: 元忠辭氣不屈，思止怒而倒曳元忠。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong's words and spirit did not yield; Sizhi in anger dragged Yuanzhong upside down.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong would not bend in word or spirit. Enraged, Sizhi seized him and dragged him head downward.

sentences.zh: 元忠徐起曰：「我薄命，如乘惡驢墜，腳為鐙所掛，被拖曳。」

translations.literal: Yuanzhong slowly rose and said: "I am ill-fated, like falling from a vicious donkey with my foot caught in the stirrup, being dragged along."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong slowly got up and said: "I am ill-fated—as when one falls from a vicious donkey with a foot caught in the stirrup and is dragged along."

sentences.zh: 思止大怒，又曳之曰：「汝拒捍制使，奏斬之。」

translations.literal: Sizhi was greatly angered and dragged him again, saying: "You resist and defy the controlling commissioner—I will memorialize to have you beheaded."
translations.idiomatic: Sizhi flew into a greater rage and dragged him again. "You resist the inquisition commissioner. I will recommend your execution."

sentences.zh: 元忠曰：「侯思止，汝今為國家御史，須識禮數輕重。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong said: "Hou Sizhi, you are now an imperial censor; you must know the weight and light of ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong said: "Hou Sizhi, you are an imperial censor now. You ought to know the difference between propriety and disgrace.

sentences.zh: 如必須魏元忠頭，何不以鋸截將，無為抑我承反。

translations.literal: If you must have Wei Yuanzhong's head, why not use a saw to cut it off? Do not force me down to admit rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: If you must have my head, take a saw and cut it off—do not force me to confess treason.

sentences.zh: 奈何爾佩服硃紫，親銜天命，不行正直之事，乃言白司馬、孟青，是何言也！

translations.literal: How is it that you wear vermilion and purple, personally bearing Heaven's mandate, yet do not perform upright affairs, but speak of White Horse Slope and Meng Qing—what sort of talk is this!
translations.idiomatic: You wear the purple and scarlet of office and bear the mandate of Heaven—yet instead of doing what is upright, you babble about White Horse Slope and Meng Qing. What kind of talk is that?

sentences.zh: 非魏元忠，無人抑教。」

translations.literal: Were it not for Wei Yuanzhong, there would be no one to restrain and instruct you."
translations.idiomatic: Were it not for Wei Yuanzhong, no one would set you straight."

sentences.zh: 思止驚起悚怍，曰：「思止死罪，幸蒙中丞教。」

translations.literal: Sizhi started up in alarm and shame, saying: "Sizhi deserves death; I am fortunate to receive the Censor's instruction."
translations.idiomatic: Sizhi started up, alarmed and ashamed. "I deserve death," he said. "I am fortunate to receive your instruction, Lord Censor."

sentences.zh: 引上床坐而問之。

translations.literal: He led him onto the bed to sit and questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: He had Yuanzhong seated on the bed and questioned him further.

sentences.zh: 元忠徐就坐自若，思止言竟不正。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong slowly took his seat with composure; Sizhi's words in the end were not corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong calmly took his seat as if nothing had happened. Sizhi never did set the record straight.

sentences.zh: 時人效之，以為談謔之資。

translations.literal: People of the time imitated this, taking it as material for jest and banter.
translations.idiomatic: People at court imitated the exchange and turned it into gossip and amusement.

sentences.zh: 侍御史霍獻可笑之，思止以聞。

translations.literal: Attending Censor Huo Xianke laughed at it; Sizhi reported this to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Attending Censor Huo Xianke mocked the affair, and Sizhi reported it to the Empress.

sentences.zh: 則天怒，謂獻可曰：「我已用之，卿笑何也？」

translations.literal: Wu Zetian was angry and said to Xianke: "I have already employed him—why do you laugh?"
