translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu was furious. She said to Xianke: "I have already appointed him—why do you mock him?"

sentences.zh: 獻可具以其言奏，則天亦大笑。

translations.literal: Xianke fully reported their words in a memorial; Wu Zetian also laughed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Xianke reported the entire exchange. Empress Wu laughed heartily as well.

sentences.zh: 時來俊臣棄故妻，逼娶太原王慶詵女，思止亦奏請娶趙郡李自挹女，敕政事商量。

translations.literal: At that time Lai Junchen abandoned his former wife and forced marriage with the daughter of Wang Qingshen of Taiyuan; Sizhi also memorialized requesting to marry the daughter of Li Ziyi of Zhao Commandery—the order was referred to the chief ministers for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Lai Junchen had cast off his first wife and forced the daughter of Wang Qingshen of Taiyuan into marriage. Sizhi likewise petitioned to marry the daughter of Li Ziyi of Zhao Commandery. The matter was referred to the chief ministers for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 鳳閣侍郎李昭德撫掌謂諸宰相曰：「大可笑。」

translations.literal: Phoenix Pavilion Vice Minister Li Zhaode clapped his hands and said to the chief ministers: "Utterly laughable."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Li Zhaode of the Phoenix Pavilion clapped his hands and told the chief ministers: "This is absurd."

sentences.zh: 諸宰相問故，昭德曰：「往年來俊臣賊劫王慶詵女，已大辱國。

translations.literal: The chief ministers asked the reason; Zhaode said: "In past years Lai Junchen robbed and seized Wang Qingshen's daughter—a great disgrace to the state.
translations.idiomatic: When the chief ministers asked why, Zhaode said: "Last year Lai Junchen plundered Wang Qingshen's daughter—that already shamed the realm.

sentences.zh: 今日此奴又請索李自挹女，無乃復辱國乎！」

translations.literal: Today this slave again requests to seize Li Ziyi's daughter—is this not again shaming the state!"
translations.idiomatic: Now this wretch asks for Li Ziyi's daughter as well. Will the realm suffer disgrace a second time?"

sentences.zh: 竟為李昭德搒殺之。

translations.literal: In the end he was beaten to death by Li Zhaode.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Li Zhaode had him beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 萬國俊，洛陽人。

translations.literal: Wan Guojun—Wan Guojun was a man of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Guojun was a native of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 少譎異險詐。

translations.literal: From youth he was strange, devious, dangerous, and deceitful.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was cunning, treacherous, and deceitful.

sentences.zh: 垂拱後，與來俊臣同為《羅織經》，屠覆宗枝朝貴，以作威勢。

translations.literal: After the Chuigong era, together with Lai Junchen he co-authored the "Classic of Framing," slaughtering and overturning imperial clansmen and court nobles to wield threatening power.
translations.idiomatic: After the Chuigong era he and Lai Junchen co-authored the Classic of Fabricating Charges, destroying imperial clansmen and high officials to build their own terror.

sentences.zh: 自司刑評事，俊臣同引為判官，

translations.literal: From the post of Legal Review Aide, Junchen jointly brought him in as judge-assistant,
translations.idiomatic: Starting as a legal review aide, Junchen brought him in as an assistant judge.

sentences.zh: 天授二年，攝右臺監察御史，常與俊臣同按制獄。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianshou, he acted as Investigating Censor of the Right Censorate, and he often joined Junchen in investigating controlled prisons.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianshou, he served as acting Investigating Censor of the Right Censorate and often joined Junchen in running the inquisition prisons.

sentences.zh: 長壽二年，有上封事言嶺南流人有陰謀逆者，乃遣國俊就按之，若得反狀，便斬決。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changshou, someone submitted a sealed memorial saying exiles in Lingnan had secret plots of rebellion; Guojun was then dispatched to investigate on the spot—if evidence of rebellion was obtained, immediate execution was authorized.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Changshou, when a sealed memorial reported that exiles in Lingnan were plotting treason in secret, she dispatched Guojun to investigate. If he found evidence of rebellion, he was authorized to execute them on the spot.

sentences.zh: 國俊至廣州，遍召流人，置於別所，矯制賜自盡，並號哭稱冤不服。

translations.literal: Guojun reached Guangzhou, summoned all exiles everywhere, placed them in a separate location, forged an imperial order granting them suicide by their own hand—all wailed, crying injustice and refusing submission.
translations.idiomatic: Guojun reached Guangzhou, summoned every exile, and confined them separately. Forging an imperial order, he granted them "suicide." All wept, protesting their innocence and refusing to comply.

sentences.zh: 國俊乃引出，擁之水曲，以次加戮，三百餘人，一時並命。

translations.literal: Guojun then led them out, pushed them to a bend of the water, and in succession applied slaughter—more than three hundred men, all their lives taken at once.
translations.idiomatic: Guojun then marched them out, drove them to a bend in the river, and killed them one after another—more than three hundred men put to death in a single massacre.

sentences.zh: 然後鍛煉，曲成反狀，仍誣奏云：「諸流人咸有怨望，若不推究，為變不遙。」

translations.literal: Then he forged evidence, twisting to complete a treason case, and still falsely memorialized, saying: "All the exiles harbor resentment; if not thoroughly investigated, rebellion is not far off."
translations.idiomatic: Only then did he torture confessions out of survivors and fabricated a treason case, memorializing falsely: "All the exiles harbor resentment. Unless this is investigated thoroughly, rebellion is imminent."

sentences.zh: 則天深然其奏，乃命右衛翊二府兵曹參軍劉光業、司刑評事王德壽、苑南面監丞鮑思恭、尚輦直長王大貞、右武衛兵曹參軍屈貞筠等，並攝監察御史，分往劍南、黔中、安南等六道鞫流人。

translations.literal: Wu Zetian deeply approved his memorial and ordered Youwei Yi Second Office Military Staff Officer Liu Guangye, Legal Review Aide Wang Deshou, Garden South Supervisor Assistant Bao Sigong, Palace Transport Direct Officer Wang Dazhen, Youwuwei Military Staff Officer Qu Zhenyun, and others—all acting as Investigating Censors—to go separately to six circuits including Jiannan, Qianzhong, and Annam to interrogate exiles.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu was deeply persuaded and ordered Liu Guangye, Wang Deshou, Bao Sigong, Wang Dazhen, Qu Zhenyun, and others—all appointed acting Investigating Censors—to fan out across six circuits including Jiannan, Qianzhong, and Annam to interrogate exiles.

sentences.zh: 尋擢授國俊朝散大夫、肅政臺侍御史。

translations.literal: Soon Guojun was promoted and appointed Grand Master of Palace Leisure and Attending Censor of the Su Politics Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Guojun was promoted to Grand Master of Palace Leisure and Attending Censor of the Su Politics Censorate.

sentences.zh: 光業等見國俊盛行殘殺，得加榮貴，乃共肆其兇忍，唯恐後之。

translations.literal: Guangye and the others saw Guojun through rampant slaughter gain glory and nobility; they then together unleashed their vicious cruelty, each fearing to fall behind.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Guojun had won rank and riches through wholesale slaughter, Guangye and the others competed in savagery, each afraid of being outdone.

sentences.zh: 光業殺九百人，德壽殺七百人，其餘少者咸五百人。

translations.literal: Guangye killed nine hundred men; Deshou killed seven hundred; the rest, at the least, all five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Guangye killed nine hundred people, Deshou seven hundred, and the others no fewer than five hundred each.

sentences.zh: 亦有遠年流人，非革命時犯罪，亦同殺之。

translations.literal: There were also exiles from distant years who had not committed crimes at the time of the revolution—they were likewise killed.
translations.idiomatic: Some had been exiled years earlier for offenses unrelated to the dynastic transition; they were killed just the same.

sentences.zh: 則天後知其冤濫，下制：「被六道使所殺之家口未歸者，並遞還本管。」

translations.literal: Wu Zetian afterward learned of the injustice and excess, and issued an edict: "Families of those killed by the Six-Circuit Commissioners whose household members have not returned—all are to be sent back in relay to their original jurisdictions."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu later learned how unjust the killings had been and issued an edict: "Household members of those slain by the Six-Circuit Commissioners who have not yet returned home are to be sent back to their native districts."

sentences.zh: 國俊等俄亦相次而死，皆見鬼物為祟，或有流竄而終。

translations.literal: Guojun and the others soon also died one after another—all saw ghostly apparitions haunting them, or ended by exile and banishment.
translations.idiomatic: Guojun and the others soon died one after another as well—some claiming to be haunted by ghosts, others dying in exile.

sentences.zh: 來子珣，雍州長安人。

translations.literal: Lai Zixun—Lai Zixun was a native of Chang'an in Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Zixun was a native of Chang'an in Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 永昌元年四月，以上書陳事，除左臺監察御史。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Yongchang, for submitting a memorial stating affairs, he was appointed Left Censorate Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Yongchang, he was appointed Investigating Censor of the Left Censorate for submitting a memorial on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 時朝士有不帶靴而朝者，子珣彈之曰：「臣聞束帶立於朝。」

translations.literal: At that time there were court officials who attended court without wearing boots; Zixun impeached them, saying: "I have heard that one girds oneself and stands in court."
translations.idiomatic: When some court officials appeared at court without wearing boots, Zixun impeached them, saying: "I have heard that one should attend court properly girded and capped."

sentences.zh: 舉朝大噱。

translations.literal: The whole court roared with laughter.
translations.idiomatic: The entire court burst into laughter.

sentences.zh: 則天委之按制獄，多希旨，賜姓姓武氏，字家臣。

translations.literal: Wu Zetian entrusted him with investigating controlled prisons; he often matched her intent; she granted him the surname Wu and the courtesy name Jiachén (House Servant).
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu put him in charge of the inquisition prisons. Eager to please her, he was granted the surname Wu and the courtesy name Jiachén—"House Servant."

sentences.zh: 天授中，丁父憂，起復朝散大夫、侍御史。

translations.literal: In the Tianshou era, upon his father's death he was recalled from mourning to serve as Grand Master of Palace Leisure and Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianshou era, when his father died he was recalled from mourning and appointed Grand Master of Palace Leisure and Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 時雅州剌史劉行實及弟渠州刺史行瑜、尚衣奉御行威並兄子鷹揚郎將軍虔通等，為子珣誣告謀反誅，又於盱眙毀其父左監門大將軍伯英棺柩。

translations.literal: At that time Ya Prefecture Prefect Liu Xingshi, his younger brother Qu Prefecture Prefect Xingyu, Court Dress Director Xingwei, and elder brother's son Eagle-Wielding General Qiantong and others were falsely denounced by Zixun for plotting rebellion and executed; he also destroyed at Xuyi the coffin of their father, Left Gate General Boying.
translations.idiomatic: Zixun falsely accused Ya Prefecture Prefect Liu Xingshi, his brother Qu Prefecture Prefect Xingyu, Court Dress Director Xingwei, and their nephew Eagle-Wielding General Qiantong of treason and had them executed. He also desecrated the coffin of their father, Left Gate General Boying, at Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 俄又轉為遊擊將軍、右羽林中郎將。

translations.literal: Soon he was again transferred to Mobile General and Right Wings Forest Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was reassigned as Mobile General and Right General of the Feathered Forest Guard.

sentences.zh: 常衣錦半臂，言笑自若，朝士誚之。

translations.literal: He constantly wore brocade half-sleeves, speaking and laughing at ease; court officials derided him.
translations.idiomatic: He often wore brocade vests and carried on as if nothing were amiss, to the scorn of the court.

sentences.zh: 長壽元年，配流愛州卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changshou, he was sentenced to exile in Ai Prefecture and died there.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Changshou he was exiled to Ai Prefecture, where he died.

sentences.zh: 王弘義，冀州衡水人也。

translations.literal: Wang Hongyi—Wang Hongyi was a native of Hengshui in Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hongyi was a native of Hengshui in Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 告變，授遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: For reporting a plot, he was appointed Mobile General.
translations.idiomatic: For reporting a treasonous plot, he was appointed Mobile General.

sentences.zh: 天授中，拜右臺殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: In the Tianshou era, he was appointed Right Censorate Palace Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianshou era he was appointed Palace Attending Censor of the Right Censorate.

sentences.zh: 長壽中，拜左臺侍御史，與來俊臣羅告衣冠，

translations.literal: In the Changshou era, he was appointed Left Censorate Attending Censor; with Lai Junchen he framed and denounced the gentry and officials,
translations.idiomatic: During the Changshou era he was appointed Attending Censor of the Left Censorate and joined Lai Junchen in fabricating charges against officials and scholars.

sentences.zh: 延載元年，俊臣貶，弘義亦流放瓊州，妄稱敕追。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanzai, when Junchen was demoted, Hongyi was also exiled to Qiong Prefecture; he falsely claimed an imperial order summoning him back.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanzai, When Junchen was demoted, Hongyi was also exiled to Qiong Prefecture, where he falsely claimed an imperial summons had recalled him.

sentences.zh: 時胡元禮為侍御史，使嶺南道，次於襄、鄧，會而按之。

translations.literal: At that time Hu Yuanli was Attending Censor, on mission to the Lingnan circuit; stopping at Xiang and Deng, he encountered and investigated him.
translations.idiomatic: Attending Censor Hu Yuanli was then on assignment in Lingnan. Passing through Xiang and Deng, he intercepted Hongyi and investigated the case.

sentences.zh: 弘義詞窮，乃謂曰：「與公氣類。」

translations.literal: Hongyi's words were exhausted; he then said to him: "We are kindred in spirit."
translations.idiomatic: At a loss for words, Hongyi said: "You and I are birds of a feather."

sentences.zh: 元禮曰：「足下任御史，元禮任洛陽尉。

translations.literal: Yuanli said: "When you were Attending Censor, Yuanli was Luoyang District Captain.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli replied: "When you served as censor, I was a Luoyang district captain.

sentences.zh: 元禮今為御史，公乃流囚，復何氣類？」

translations.literal: Yuanli is now Attending Censor; you are an exiled prisoner—what kind of kindred spirit?"
translations.idiomatic: Now I am the censor and you are the exile. What kind of kindred spirit are we?"

sentences.zh: 乃搒殺之。

translations.literal: Then he had him beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Hongyi beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 弘義每暑月系囚，必於小房中積蒿而施氈褥，遭之者斯須氣絕矣。

translations.literal: Every summer month Hongyi imprisoned captives, he invariably piled wormwood in a small room and laid felt mattresses over it; those who suffered this would within moments lose breath and die.
translations.idiomatic: In summer Hongyi confined prisoners in small rooms stuffed with wormwood and covered with felt mats; victims suffocated within moments.

sentences.zh: 茍自誣引，則易於他房。

translations.literal: If one falsely implicated oneself in confession, then one was moved to another room.
translations.idiomatic: If a prisoner falsely implicated others, he was moved to a more tolerable cell.

sentences.zh: 與俊臣常行移牒，州縣懾懼，自矜曰：「我之文牒，有如狼毒野葛也。」

translations.literal: With Junchen he frequently issued transfer documents; prefectures and counties were fearful and awed; he prided himself, saying: "My official documents are like wolf's bane and wild kudzu."
translations.idiomatic: He and Junchen routinely sent out summonses that struck prefectures and counties with terror. He boasted: "My documents are poison—wolf's bane and wild kudzu."

sentences.zh: 弘義常於鄉里傍舍求瓜，主吝之，弘義乃狀言瓜園中有白兔，縣官命人捕逐，斯須園苗盡矣。

translations.literal: Hongyi often sought melons from a neighbor's garden in his village; the owner was stingy; Hongyi then filed a report saying there was a white rabbit in the melon garden—the county officials ordered men to hunt and chase it, and in moments all the garden seedlings were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Hongyi once wanted melons from a neighbor's garden; when the owner refused, he reported that a white rabbit was hiding in the patch. County officials sent men to hunt it, and within moments the entire crop was trampled flat.

sentences.zh: 內史李昭德曰：「昔聞蒼鷹獄吏，今見白免御史。」

translations.literal: Inner Secretary Li Zhaode said: "Formerly one heard of the Blue Falcon prison clerk; now one sees the White Rabbit Censor."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Li Zhaode remarked: "People once spoke of the 'Blue Falcon' jailer; now we have a 'White Rabbit' censor."

sentences.zh: 郭霸，廬江人也。

translations.literal: Guo Ba—Guo Ba was a native of Lujiang,
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ba was a native of Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 天授二年，自宋州寧陵丞應革命舉，拜左臺監察御史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianshou, from Assistant Magistrate of Ningling in Song Prefecture, he responded to the Revolutionary Examinations and was appointed Left Censorate Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianshou, starting as assistant magistrate of Ningling in Song Prefecture, he entered office through the special examinations held at the founding of the new regime and was appointed Investigating Censor of the Left Censorate.

sentences.zh: 如意元年，除左臺殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Ruyi, he was appointed Left Censorate Palace Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Ruyi, he was appointed Palace Attending Censor of the Left Censorate.

sentences.zh: 長壽二年，右臺侍御史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changshou, he became Right Censorate Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Changshou, he became Attending Censor of the Right Censorate.

sentences.zh: 初舉集，召見，於則天前自陳忠鯁云：「往年征徐敬業，臣願抽其筋，食其肉，飲其血，絕其髓。」

translations.literal: At the first examination gathering, summoned for audience, before Wu Zetian he declared his loyal bluntness, saying: "In past years when campaigning against Xu Jingye, I wished to pull out his sinews, eat his flesh, drink his blood, and exhaust his marrow."
translations.idiomatic: At his first examination audience before Empress Wu, he proclaimed his zeal, saying: "When Xu Jingye was put down, I wanted to tear out his sinews, eat his flesh, drink his blood, and drain his marrow to the last drop."

sentences.zh: 則天悅，故拜焉，時人號為「四其御史」。

translations.literal: Wu Zetian was pleased; therefore he was appointed; people of the time called him the "Four-His Censor."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu was delighted and appointed him. People nicknamed him the "Four-His Censor."

sentences.zh: 時大夫魏元忠臥疾，諸御史盡往省之，霸獨居後。

translations.literal: At that time Senior Censor Wei Yuanzhong lay ill; all the censors went to visit him; Ba alone stayed behind.
translations.idiomatic: When Senior Censor Wei Yuanzhong fell ill, all the other censors visited him—Ba alone lingered behind.

sentences.zh: 比見元忠，憂懼，請示元忠便液，以驗疾之輕重。

translations.literal: When he saw Yuanzhong, anxious and fearful, he requested to examine Yuanzhong's urine and stool to verify the severity of the illness.
translations.idiomatic: When he finally saw Yuanzhong, feigning concern, he asked to inspect his urine and stool to judge how serious the illness was.

sentences.zh: 元忠驚悚，霸悅曰：「大夫糞味甘，或不瘳。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong was alarmed; Ba said with pleasure: "The Senior Censor's stool tastes sweet—perhaps he will not recover.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong was horrified. Ba declared cheerfully: "Your stool tastes sweet—you may not recover.

sentences.zh: 今味苦，當即愈矣。」

translations.literal: Now the taste is bitter—he should soon recover."
translations.idiomatic: But now it tastes bitter—you should recover soon."

sentences.zh: 元忠剛直，殊惡之，以其事露朝士。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong, upright and unyielding, deeply hated this; he exposed the matter to court officials.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong, ever blunt and upright, was revolted and spread the story among the court.

sentences.zh: 嘗推芳州刺史李思徵，搒捶考禁，不勝而死。

translations.literal: Once investigating Fang Prefecture Prefect Li Sizheng, he beat and tortured him in examination and confinement; unable to bear it, Sizheng died.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while investigating Fang Prefecture Prefect Li Sizheng, he beat and tortured him until the man died under interrogation.

sentences.zh: 聖歷中，屢見思徵，甚惡之。

translations.literal: In the Shengli era, he repeatedly saw Sizheng; he deeply hated it.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shengli era he kept seeing Sizheng's ghost and was terrified.

sentences.zh: 嘗因退朝遽歸，命家人曰：「速請僧轉經設齋。」

translations.literal: Once, upon returning hurriedly after leaving court, he ordered his household: "Quickly summon monks to recite sutras and hold a vegetarian feast."
translations.idiomatic: Once, rushing home after court, he ordered his household: "Summon monks at once for sutra recitation and a ritual feast."

sentences.zh: 須臾見思徵從數十騎上其廷，曰：「汝枉陷我，我今取汝。」

translations.literal: In a moment he saw Sizheng with several dozen riders ascend his courtyard, saying: "You falsely trapped me—today I take you."
translations.idiomatic: Moments later he saw Sizheng ride into his courtyard at the head of several dozen horsemen, saying: "You framed me unjustly. I have come for you now."

sentences.zh: 霸周章惶怖，援刀自刳其腹，斯須蛆爛矣。

translations.literal: Ba flustered and terrified, seized a knife and ripped open his own belly; in moments maggots swarmed and he rotted.
translations.idiomatic: Panicked, Ba grabbed a knife and gutted himself. Within moments his entrails were crawling with maggots.

sentences.zh: 是日，閭里亦見兵馬數十騎駐於門，少頃不復見矣。

translations.literal: That day, in the lanes the people also saw several dozen riders of soldiers and horses stationed at the gate; after a little while they were no longer seen.
translations.idiomatic: That same day neighbors also saw several dozen mounted soldiers halt at his gate—and a moment later they vanished.

sentences.zh: 時洛陽橋壞，行李弊之，至是功畢。

translations.literal: At that time the Luoyang Bridge was broken; Li Xingbi was put in charge of it; by now the work was completed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Luoyang Bridge had fallen into disrepair; Li Xingbi was assigned to repair it, and by then the work was finished.

sentences.zh: 則天嘗問群臣：「比在外有何好事？」

translations.literal: Empress Wu once asked the ministers: "What good news has there been outside lately?"
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu once asked her ministers: "What good tidings have you heard from beyond the palace lately?"

sentences.zh: 舍人張元一素滑稽，對曰：「百姓喜洛橋成，幸郭霸死，此即好事。」

translations.literal: Attendant Gentleman Zhang Yuanyi, known for his wit, replied: "The people rejoice that the Luo Bridge is finished and are glad that Guo Ba is dead—that is good news."
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Gentleman Zhang Yuanyi, a born wit, answered: "The people are pleased the Luo Bridge is done and overjoyed that Guo Ba is dead—that is the good news."

sentences.zh: 吉頊吉頊，洛州河南人也。

translations.literal: Ji Shu—Ji Shu was a native of Henan in Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Shu was a native of Henan in Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 身長七尺，陰毒敢言事。

translations.literal: He stood seven chi tall; ruthless and bold in denouncing matters.
translations.idiomatic: He stood seven feet in height, venomous in temperament and bold in bringing accusations.

sentences.zh: 進士舉，累轉明堂尉，

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was promoted through successive posts to Mingtang Commandant,
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and rose through a series of posts to become Commandant of the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 萬歲通天二年，有箕州刺史劉思禮，自云學於張憬藏，善相，云洛州錄事參軍綦連耀應圖讖，有「兩角騏麟兒」之符命。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wansui Tongtian, there was Jizhou Prefect Liu Sili, who claimed to have studied under Zhang Jingzang and was skilled at physiognomy; he said that Luozhou Administrative Assistant Qi Lianyao fulfilled a prophecy in charts and auguries, bearing the destined sign of "a qilin colt with two horns."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wansui Tongtian, There was Jizhou Prefect Liu Sili, who claimed to have studied physiognomy under Zhang Jingzang and declared that Lu Prefecture Administrative Assistant Qi Lianyao matched a prophecy, bearing the destined omen of "a qilin foal with two horns."

sentences.zh: 頊告之，則天付武懿宗與頊對訊。

translations.literal: Shu reported it; Empress Wu assigned Wu Yizong and Shu to conduct the interrogation jointly.
translations.idiomatic: Shu reported the matter, and Empress Wu had Wu Yizong and Shu conduct the joint interrogation.

sentences.zh: 懿宗與頊誘思禮，令廣引朝士，必全其命。

translations.literal: Yizong and Shu tempted Sili, ordering him to implicate many court officials broadly, and promising that his life would certainly be spared.
translations.idiomatic: Yizong and Shu coaxed Sili with a promise: implicate as many court officials as he could, and his life would be spared.

sentences.zh: 思禮乃引鳳閣侍郎李元素、夏官侍郎孫元通、天官侍郎劉奇、石抱忠、鳳閣舍人王處、來庭、主簿柳璆、給事中周潘、涇州刺史王勔、監察御史王助、司議郎路敬淳、司門員外郎劉慎之、右司員外郎宇文全志等三十六家，微有忤意者，必構之，楚毒百端，以成其獄。

translations.literal: Sili then implicated thirty-six families including Vice Director of the Phoenix Pavilion Li Yuansu, Vice Director of the Summer Office Sun Yuantong, Vice Director of the Celestial Office Liu Qi, Shi Baozhong, Phoenix Pavilion Attendant Gentleman Wang Chu, Lai Ting, Registrar Liu Yao, Supervising Attendant Zhou Pan, Jing Prefecture Prefect Wang Xu, Investigation Censor Wang Zhu, Reviewing Secretary Lu Jingchun, Vice Director of the Gate Office Liu Shenzhi, Vice Director of the Right Office Yuwen Quanzhi, and others. Whenever anyone slightly displeased them, they would fabricate charges; torture took every form, until their case was complete.
translations.idiomatic: Sili then implicated thirty-six households—among them Vice Director Li Yuansu of the Phoenix Pavilion, Vice Director Sun Yuantong of the Summer Office, Vice Director Liu Qi of the Celestial Office, Shi Baozhong, Attendant Gentlemen Wang Chu and Lai Ting of the Phoenix Pavilion, Registrar Liu Yao, Supervising Attendant Zhou Pan, Jing Prefecture Prefect Wang Xu, Investigation Censor Wang Zhu, Reviewing Secretary Lu Jingchun, Vice Director of the Gate Office Liu Shenzhi, Vice Director of the Right Office Yuwen Quanzhi, and others. Whoever slightly crossed them was framed; every torture was applied until the case was fixed.

sentences.zh: 皆海內賢士名家，天下冤之，親故連累竄逐者千餘人。

translations.literal: All were worthy men and famous families from throughout the realm; the empire considered it a great injustice; relatives and associates implicated and banished numbered more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: They were all distinguished scholars and eminent families from across the empire; the world deemed it an outrage, and more than a thousand kin and associates were implicated and exiled.

sentences.zh: 頊由是擢拜右肅政臺中丞，日見恩遇。

translations.literal: Shu was therefore promoted and appointed Senior Censor of the Right Pure Administration Censorate, and day by day won favor.
translations.idiomatic: For this Shu was promoted to Senior Censor of the Right Pure Administration Censorate and daily gained greater favor.

sentences.zh: 明年，突厥寇陷趙、定等州。

translations.literal: The next year, the Turks raided and captured Zhao, Ding, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Turkic raiders overran Zhao, Ding, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 則天召頊檢校相州刺史，以斷賊南侵之路。

translations.literal: Empress Wu summoned Shu and appointed him acting Prefect of Xiangzhou to block the enemy's route of southern invasion.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu summoned Shu and named him acting Prefect of Xiang Prefecture to cut off the raiders' southern advance.

sentences.zh: 頊以素不習武為辭，則天曰：「賊勢將退，藉卿威名鎮遏耳。」

translations.literal: Shu declined on the grounds that he was wholly unused to military affairs. Empress Wu said: "The enemy's strength is about to retreat—it is merely to borrow your prestige to deter them."
translations.idiomatic: Shu pleaded that he had no training in military affairs. Empress Wu replied: "The raiders are about to withdraw; I only need your name to hold them in check."

sentences.zh: 初，太原有術士溫彬茂，高宗時老，臨死，封一狀謂其妻曰：「吾死後，年名垂拱，即詣闕獻之，慎勿開也。」

translations.literal: Initially, in Taiyuan there was a diviner named Wen Binmao. In the Gaozong era he grew old; on the verge of death he sealed a document and told his wife: "After I die, when the era name is Chuigong, go to the palace and present it—be careful not to open it."
translations.idiomatic: At first there was a diviner in Taiyuan named Wen Binmao. In Emperor Gaozong's reign he grew old; as death approached he sealed a document and told his wife: "After I die, when the era name becomes Chuigong, take this to court and present it—but do not open it."

sentences.zh: 垂拱初，其妻獻之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chuigong era, his wife presented it.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Chuigong era, his wife presented it at court.

sentences.zh: 狀中預陳則天革命及突厥至趙、定之事，故則天知賊至趙州而退。

translations.literal: The document in advance set forth Empress Wu's revolution and the Turks' arrival at Zhao and Ding; therefore Empress Wu knew the enemy would reach Zhaozhou and then withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The document foretold Empress Wu's seizure of power and the Turks' advance on Zhao and Ding; thus Empress Wu knew the raiders would reach Zhao Prefecture and then withdraw.

sentences.zh: 頊初至州募人，略無應者。

translations.literal: When Shu first arrived at the prefecture and recruited men, scarcely anyone responded.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu first reached the prefecture and tried to recruit troops, almost no one answered the call.

sentences.zh: 俄而詔以皇太子為元帥，應募者不可勝數。

translations.literal: Before long an edict came making the Crown Prince supreme commander, and volunteers became too numerous to count.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict named the Crown Prince supreme commander, and recruits poured in beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 及賊退，頊入朝奏之，則天甚悅。

translations.literal: When the enemy withdrew, Shu entered court and reported it; Empress Wu was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: After the raiders withdrew, Shu returned to court with his report, and Empress Wu was delighted.

sentences.zh: 聖歷二年臘月，遷天官侍郎、同鳳閣鸞臺平章事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Shengli, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Celestial Office and made Associate Director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the second year of Shengli, he was appointed Vice Director of the Celestial Office and Associate Director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.

sentences.zh: 時易之、昌宗諷則天置控鶴監官員，則天以易之為控鶴監。

translations.literal: At that time Yizhi and Changzong urged Empress Wu to establish posts in the Crane-Control Office; Empress Wu made Yizhi its commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhang Yizhi and Zhang Changzong urged Empress Wu to create posts in the Crane-Control Office, and she made Yizhi its commissioner.

sentences.zh: 頊素與易之兄弟親善，遂引頊，以殿中少監田歸道、鳳閣舍人薛稷、正諫大夫員半千、夏官侍郎李迥秀，俱為控鶴內供奉，時議甚不悅。

translations.literal: Shu had long been on friendly terms with the Yizhi brothers; he therefore brought Shu in, along with Palace Supervisor Tian Guidao, Phoenix Pavilion Attendant Gentleman Xue Ji, Remonstrance Grand Master Yuan Banqian, and Vice Director of the Summer Office Li Jiongxiu—all as Inner Attendants of the Crane-Control Office; public opinion was deeply displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Shu had long been close to the Zhang brothers, and they brought him in along with Palace Supervisor Tian Guidao, Attendant Gentleman Xue Ji of the Phoenix Pavilion, Remonstrance Grand Master Yuan Banqian, and Vice Director Li Jiongxiu of the Summer Office—all as Inner Attendants of the Crane-Control Office, to widespread disapproval.

sentences.zh: 初，則天以頊幹辯有口才，偉儀質，堪委以心腹，故擢任之。

translations.literal: Initially Empress Wu considered Shu capable in debate and eloquent, with an imposing bearing, fit to be entrusted as a trusted confidant; therefore she promoted and employed him.
translations.idiomatic: At first Empress Wu valued Shu for his quick wit, eloquence, and imposing presence, and considered him fit for her inner circle; that was why she promoted him.

sentences.zh: 及與武懿宗爭趙州功於殿中，懿宗短小俯僂，頊聲氣淩厲，下視懿宗，嘗不相假。

translations.literal: When he contended with Wu Yizong in the palace over credit for Zhao Prefecture, Yizong was short and stooped; Shu's voice and manner were fierce and overbearing; he looked down on Yizong and often showed him no indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: When he disputed Wu Yizong in court over credit for the victory at Zhao Prefecture, Yizong was short and bent; Shu spoke in a sharp, domineering tone and looked down on him, rarely showing any deference.

sentences.zh: 則天以為：「卑我諸武於我前，其可倚與！」

translations.literal: Empress Wu thought: "He humiliates my Wu clan before me—how can he be relied upon!"
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu concluded: "He humiliates my Wu kinsmen to my face—how can I rely on him!"

sentences.zh: 其年十月，以弟作偽官，貶琰川尉，後改安固尉。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year, because his younger brother had held a counterfeit office, he was demoted to Commandant of Yan River and later changed to Commandant of Angu.
translations.idiomatic: That tenth month, because his younger brother had held a forged office, he was demoted to Commandant of Yan River and later reassigned as Commandant of Angu.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died.

sentences.zh: 初，中宗未立為皇太子時，易之、昌宗嘗密問頊自安之策。

translations.literal: Initially, before Zhongzong was established as Crown Prince, Yizhi and Changzong once secretly asked Shu for a strategy to secure themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, before Zhongzong was named Crown Prince, Zhang Yizhi and Zhang Changzong had secretly asked Shu how they might secure their own safety.

sentences.zh: 頊云：「公兄弟承恩既深，非有大功於天下，則不全矣。

translations.literal: Shu said: "You brothers have received favor so deeply that unless you perform great service for the realm, you will not survive intact.
translations.idiomatic: Shu said: "You brothers have enjoyed the deepest favor; unless you win great merit for the empire, you will not keep your heads.

sentences.zh: 今天下士庶，咸思李家，廬陵既在房州，相王又在幽閉，主上春秋既高，須有付托。

translations.literal: Today the scholars and common people throughout the realm all long for the Li house; the Prince of Luling is already in Fang Prefecture, and the Prince of Xiang remains in close confinement; the sovereign's years are already advanced—there must be a hand to receive the trust.
translations.idiomatic: All the people under heaven now yearn for the House of Li; the Prince of Luling is at Fang Prefecture and the Prince of Xiang remains under close guard; Your Majesty's years are advanced, and the throne must pass to someone worthy of trust.

sentences.zh: 武氏諸王，殊非屬意。

translations.literal: The princes of the Wu clan are by no means the object of their hopes.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu princes are not whom the people have in mind.

sentences.zh: 明公若能從容請建立廬陵及相王，以副生人之望，豈止轉禍為福，必長享茅土之重矣！」

translations.literal: If you, my lords, can tactfully petition to establish the Prince of Luling and the Prince of Xiang, fulfilling the people's hopes, would you not only turn calamity into fortune—you would surely enjoy the weight of fiefdoms for long years!"
translations.idiomatic: If you can tactfully petition to restore the Prince of Luling and the Prince of Xiang, fulfilling the people's hopes, you will not merely turn disaster into blessing—you will secure great fiefs for years to come!"

sentences.zh: 易之然其言，遂承間奏請。

translations.literal: Yizhi agreed with his words and therefore seized an opportunity to present the petition.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhang brothers accepted his advice and seized a suitable moment to petition the empress.

sentences.zh: 則天知頊首謀，召而問之。

translations.literal: Empress Wu knew Shu had masterminded it and summoned him to question him.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu knew Shu had devised the plan and summoned him to account for it.

sentences.zh: 頊曰：「廬陵王及相王，皆陛下之子，先帝顧托於陛下，當有主意，唯陛下裁之。」

translations.literal: Shu said: "The Prince of Luling and the Prince of Xiang are both Your Majesty's sons; the late emperor entrusted them to Your Majesty—you should have your own judgment; let Your Majesty alone decide."
translations.idiomatic: Shu said: "The Prince of Luling and the Prince of Xiang are both Your Majesty's sons; the late emperor entrusted them to you—this is for Your Majesty alone to decide."

sentences.zh: 則天意乃定。

translations.literal: Empress Wu's mind was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu's mind was made up.

sentences.zh: 頊既得罪，時無知者。

translations.literal: After Shu fell from favor, at the time no one knew of this.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu fell from grace, no one knew what he had done.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，左右發明其事，乃下制曰：「故吏部侍郎、同中書門下平章事吉頊，體識宏遠，風規久大。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, those close to him brought the matter to light; an edict was then issued, saying: "The late Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Associate Director of the Chancellery Ji Shu possessed broad vision and enduring moral stature.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong ascended the throne, his intimates revealed what had happened, and an edict was issued: "The late Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Associate Director of the Chancellery Ji Shu was a man of far-reaching vision and enduring moral stature.

sentences.zh: 嘗以經緯之才，允膺匡佐之委。

translations.literal: He once, with his talent for statecraft, fully answered the charge of assisting in governance.
translations.idiomatic: He had once applied his talent for statecraft to the work of governance.

sentences.zh: 時王命中否，人謀未輯，首陳返政之議，克副祈天之基。

translations.literal: When the royal mandate faltered and human counsel had not yet coalesced, he was first to propose restoring the dynasty, fulfilling the foundation of prayer to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial succession hung in the balance and counsel had not yet converged, he was the first to urge restoration of the Tang house, fulfilling the dynasty's mandate from Heaven.

sentences.zh: 永懷遺烈，寧忘厥效。

translations.literal: Ever cherishing his departed merit, how could one forget his achievement?
translations.idiomatic: His departed merit should never be forgotten.

sentences.zh: 可贈左御史臺大夫。」

translations.literal: He may be posthumously awarded Grand Censor of the Left Censorate."
translations.idiomatic: He is posthumously awarded the title Grand Censor of the Left Censorate."

sentences.zh: 姚紹之姚紹之，湖州武康人也。

translations.literal: Yao Shaozhi—Yao Shaozhi was a native of Wukang in Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shaozhi was a native of Wukang in Hu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 解褐典儀，累拜監察御史。

translations.literal: Upon entering office he served as Master of Ceremonies; through successive promotions he was appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as Master of Ceremonies and rose through successive posts to Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 中宗朝，武三思恃庶人勢，駙馬都尉王同皎謀誅之。

translations.literal: In the Zhongzong reign, Wu Sansi relied on the empress consort's power; Cavalry Commandant Wang Tongjiao plotted to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Zhongzong's reign, Wu Sansi relied on Empress Wei's influence; Cavalry Commandant Wang Tongjiao plotted to kill him.

sentences.zh: 事泄，令紹之按問而誅同皎。

translations.literal: When the plot leaked, Shaozhi was ordered to investigate and execute Tongjiao.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was exposed, Shaozhi was ordered to investigate and put Tongjiao to death.

sentences.zh: 紹之初按問同皎，張仲之、祖延慶謀衣袖中發調弩射三思，伺其便，未果。

translations.literal: When Shaozhi first investigated Tongjiao, Zhang Zhongzhi and Zu Yanqing plotted to draw crossbows from their sleeves and shoot Sansi, watching for an opportunity—but did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: While Shaozhi was investigating Tongjiao, Zhang Zhongzhi and Zu Yanqing plotted to shoot Wu Sansi with crossbows hidden in their sleeves, waiting for an opening—but failed.

sentences.zh: 宋之遜以其外妹妻延慶，曰：「今日將行何事，而以妻為？」

translations.literal: Song Zhixun, who had married his cousin's wife to Yanqing, said: "What business is to be done today, that you bring your wife?"
translations.idiomatic: Song Zhixun, who had given his cousin's wife in marriage to Yanqing, said: "What mission are you on today that you bring your wife along?"

sentences.zh: 之遜固抑與延慶，且洽其心矣。

translations.literal: Zhixun forcibly restrained Yanqing and also won over his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Song Zhixun forcibly held Yanqing back and also won him over.

sentences.zh: 之遜子曇密發之，乃敕右臺大夫李承嘉與紹之按於新開門內。

translations.literal: Zhixun's son Tan secretly reported it; an edict then ordered Grand Censor of the Right Censorate Li Chengjia and Shaozhi to investigate inside the Newly Opened Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Song Zhixun's son Tan secretly reported the plot; an edict ordered Grand Censor Li Chengjia of the Right Censorate and Shaozhi to investigate inside the Newly Opened Gate.

sentences.zh: 初，紹之將直盡其事。

translations.literal: Initially Shaozhi intended to pursue the matter to its full extent.
translations.idiomatic: At first Shaozhi meant to pursue the case to its full extent.

sentences.zh: 詔宰相李嶠等對問。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Chief Minister Li Qiao and others to join in the questioning.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Chief Minister Li Qiao and others to join the interrogation.

sentences.zh: 諸相懼三思威權，但僶俛佯不問。

translations.literal: The chief ministers feared Sansi's power; they merely bowed their heads and pretended not to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers feared Sansi's power and merely bowed their heads, feigning ignorance.

sentences.zh: 仲之、延慶言曰：「宰相中有附會三思者。」

translations.literal: Zhongzhi and Yanqing said: "Among the chief ministers there are those who colluded with Sansi."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzhi and Yanqing declared: "Some of the chief ministers are in league with Sansi."

sentences.zh: 嶠與承嘉耳言，復說誘紹之，其事乃變。

translations.literal: Qiao and Chengjia spoke in each other's ears, then again persuaded and tempted Shaozhi, and the matter changed course.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao and Chengjia whispered to each other, then pressed and coaxed Shaozhi until the case took a different turn.

sentences.zh: 遂密置人力十餘，命引仲之對問。

translations.literal: They then secretly posted more than ten strongmen and ordered Zhongzhi brought for questioning.
translations.idiomatic: They then secretly posted more than ten brawny men and had Zhongzhi summoned for questioning.

sentences.zh: 至，即為紹之所擒，塞口反接，送獄中。

translations.literal: When he arrived, Shaozhi seized him at once, gagged him and bound his arms behind him, and sent him to prison.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, Shaozhi seized him at once, gagged him, bound his arms behind his back, and sent him to prison.

sentences.zh: 紹之還，謂仲之曰：「張三，事不諧矣！」

translations.literal: Shaozhi returned and said to Zhongzhi: "Zhang Three, the affair will not succeed!"
translations.idiomatic: Shaozhi turned to Zhongzhi and said: "Zhang Three, this is not going to work!"

sentences.zh: 仲之固言三思反狀，紹之命棒之而臂折，大呼天者六七。

translations.literal: Zhongzhi stubbornly spoke of Sansi's treasonous conduct; Shaozhi ordered him beaten until his arm broke; he cried out to Heaven six or seven times.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzhi insisted on detailing Sansi's treason; Shaozhi had him beaten until his arm broke, and he cried out to Heaven six or seven times.

sentences.zh: 謂紹之曰：「反賊，臂且折矣，命已輸汝，當訴爾於天帝！」

translations.literal: He said to Shaozhi: "Traitor! My arm is already broken and my life is in your hands—you will answer for this before the Lord of Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: He shouted at Shaozhi: "Traitor! My arm is broken and my life is yours—but I will accuse you before the Lord of Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 因裂衫以束之，乃自誣反而遇誅。

translations.literal: He then tore his shirt to bind his arm and falsely confessed to rebellion, whereupon he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: He tore his shirt to bind his broken arm, then falsely confessed to rebellion and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 紹之自此神氣自若，朝廷側目。

translations.literal: From this Shaozhi was calm and self-possessed as before; the court looked askance at him.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Shaozhi remained as cool and self-assured as ever, and the court watched him with dread.

sentences.zh: 累遷左臺侍御史。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became Attending Censor of the Left Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to Attending Censor of the Left Censorate.

sentences.zh: 奉使江左，經汴州，辱錄事參軍魏傳弓。

translations.literal: On a mission to the lower Yangzi region, passing through Bian Prefecture, he insulted Administrative Assistant Wei Chuanggong.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to the lower Yangzi, he passed through Bian Prefecture and humiliated Administrative Assistant Wei Chuanggong.

sentences.zh: 尋拜監察御史。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 紹之後坐贓汙，詔傳弓按之，獲贓五千餘貫以聞，當坐死。

translations.literal: Later Shaozhi was convicted of corruption; an edict ordered Chuanggong to investigate him; more than five thousand strings of illicit goods were recovered and reported; the penalty was death.
translations.idiomatic: Later Shaozhi was convicted of corruption; an edict put Chuanggong in charge of the investigation; more than five thousand strings of stolen goods were recovered and reported, and the sentence was death.

sentences.zh: 韋庶人妹保持之，遂黜放為嶺南瓊山尉。

translations.literal: Empress Wei's younger sister protected him; he was therefore dismissed and banished as Commandant of Qiongshan in Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wei's younger sister intervened on his behalf, and he was demoted and banished to serve as Commandant of Qiongshan in Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 傳弓初按紹之，紹之在揚州，色動，謂長吏盧萬石曰：「頃辱傳弓，今為所按，紹之死矣！」

translations.literal: When Chuanggong first investigated Shaozhi, Shaozhi was in Yang Prefecture; his color changed, and he said to Chief Clerk Lu Wanshi: "I recently insulted Chuanggong; now I am under his investigation—Shaozhi is finished!"
translations.idiomatic: When Chuanggong first took up the case, Shaozhi was in Yang Prefecture; his face went pale, and he told Chief Clerk Lu Wanshi: "I humiliated Chuanggong not long ago, and now he is investigating me—I am a dead man!"

sentences.zh: 逃入西京，為萬年尉擒之，擊折其足，因授南陵令員外置，

translations.literal: He fled into the western capital and was captured by the Wannian Commandant; his foot was broken in beating, and he was then appointed Supernumerary Magistrate of Nanling,
translations.idiomatic: He fled to the western capital, was captured by the Wannian Commandant, and had his foot broken under beating; he was then given a supernumerary appointment as Magistrate of Nanling.

sentences.zh: 累轉括州長史同正員，不預知州事，死。

translations.literal: through successive promotions he became Senior Administrator of Kuozhou with the rank of regular fourth grade, but did not participate in prefectural affairs, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to Senior Administrator of Kuo Prefecture with regular fourth-rank status, but did not take part in prefectural administration, and died.

sentences.zh: 周利貞周利貞，神龍初為侍御史。

translations.literal: Zhou Lizhen—Zhou Lizhen, in the Shenlong era initially served as Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Lizhen—in the Shenlong era he first served as Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 附托權要，為桓彥範、敬暉等五王嫉之，出為嘉州司馬。

translations.literal: He attached himself to powerful patrons; Huan Yanfan, Jing Hui, and the other Five Princes resented him, and he was sent out as Military Assistant of Jia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He cultivated ties to the powerful; Huan Yanfan, Jing Hui, and the other Five Princes despised him, and he was sent out as Military Assistant of Jia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時中書舍人崔湜與桓、敬善。

translations.literal: At that time Secretariat Drafter Cui Shi was on good terms with Huan and Jing.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Secretariat Drafter Cui Shi was friendly with Huan and Jing.

sentences.zh: 武三思用事禁中，彥範憂之，托心腹於湜。

translations.literal: Wu Sansi wielded power within the palace; Yanfan was troubled by it and entrusted his inner thoughts to Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sansi held sway within the palace; Yanfan was alarmed and confided his plans to Shi.

sentences.zh: 湜反露其計於三思，為三思所中，盡流嶺南。

translations.literal: Shi instead exposed their plan to Sansi; struck by Sansi, they were all banished to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi instead betrayed their plan to Sansi; caught by Sansi, they were all exiled to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 湜勸盡殺之。

translations.literal: Shi urged that they all be killed.
translations.idiomatic: Shi urged that every one of them be killed.

sentences.zh: 以絕其歸望。

translations.literal: To cut off any hope of their return.
translations.idiomatic: The aim was to cut off any hope of their return.

sentences.zh: 三思問：「誰可使者？」

translations.literal: Sansi asked: "Who can be sent for this?"
translations.idiomatic: Sansi asked: "Who can be sent to carry this out?"

sentences.zh: 利貞即湜之表兄，因舉為此行。

translations.literal: Lizhen was Shi's cousin on his mother's side; he was therefore recommended for the mission.
translations.idiomatic: Lizhen was Shi's maternal cousin, and Shi recommended him for the mission.

sentences.zh: 利貞至，皆鴆殺之，因擢為左臺御史中丞，

translations.literal: When Lizhen arrived, he poisoned them all to death and was therefore promoted to Senior Censor of the Left Censorate,
translations.idiomatic: When Lizhen arrived, he poisoned them all and was promoted to Senior Censor of the Left Censorate.

sentences.zh: 為廣州都督。

translations.literal: he served as Military Commissioner of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as Military Commissioner of Guang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時湜為中書令，與僕射劉幽求不葉，陷幽求徙於嶺表，諷利貞殺之，為桂州都督王晙護之，逗留獲免。

translations.literal: At that time Shi was Chief Minister of the Secretariat and was at odds with Vice Director Liu Youqiu; he framed Youqiu and had him exiled to the southern frontier, then urged Lizhen to kill him; Gui Prefecture Military Commissioner Wang Jun protected him, and by delaying he escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Shi was Chief Minister of the Secretariat and at odds with Vice Director Liu Youqiu; he framed Youqiu and had him exiled to the far south, then urged Lizhen to kill him; Gui Prefecture Military Commissioner Wang Jun shielded him, and by stalling he survived.

sentences.zh: 無何，玄宗正位，利貞與薛季昶、宋之問同賜死於桂州驛。

translations.literal: Before long Emperor Xuanzong took the throne; Lizhen, together with Xue Jichang and Song Zhiwen, was likewise granted death at the Gui Prefecture post station.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, after Emperor Xuanzong took the throne, Lizhen was executed by imperial grace at the Gui Prefecture post station, together with Xue Jichang and Song Zhiwen.

sentences.zh: 王旭王旭，太原祁人也。

translations.literal: Wang Xu—Wang Xu was a native of Qi in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xu was a native of Qi in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 曾祖珪，貞觀初為侍中，尚永寧公主。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Gui, in the early Zhenguan era served as Chief Minister and married Princess Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Gui served as Chief Minister in the early Zhenguan era and married Princess Yongning.

sentences.zh: 旭解褐鴻州參軍，轉兗州兵曹。

translations.literal: Xu entered office as Adjutant of Hong Prefecture and was transferred to Military Records Officer of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xu entered service as adjutant of Hong Prefecture and was transferred to military records officer of Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 正月，張柬之、桓彥範等誅張易之、昌宗兄弟，尊立孝和皇帝。

translations.literal: In the first month, Zhang Jianzhi, Huan Yanfan, and others killed the brothers Zhang Yizhi and Changzong and enthroned Emperor Zhongzong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month, Zhang Jianzhi, Huan Yanfan, and others killed Zhang Yizhi and Zhang Changzong and enthroned Emperor Zhongzong.

sentences.zh: 其兄昌儀先貶乾封尉，旭斬之，賫其首，赴於東都。

translations.literal: Xu's elder brother Changyi had first been demoted to Commandant of Qianfeng; Xu beheaded him, carried his head, and hastened to the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xu's elder brother Changyi had already been demoted to Commandant of Qianfeng; Xu beheaded him, took his head, and raced to the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 遷并州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Administrative Assistant of Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Administrative Assistant of Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 唐隆元年，玄宗誅韋庶人等。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tanglong, Emperor Xuanzong executed Empress Wei and her faction.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Tanglong era, Emperor Xuanzong executed Empress Wei and her faction.

sentences.zh: 并州長史周仁軌，韋氏之黨，有詔誅之。

translations.literal: Bing Prefecture Senior Administrator Zhou Rengui, a partisan of the Wei clan, was under edict to be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Bing Prefecture Senior Administrator Zhou Rengui, a partisan of the Wei faction, was under edict for execution.

sentences.zh: 旭不覆敕，又斬其首，馳赴西京，

translations.literal: Xu did not await confirmation of the edict; he again beheaded him and galloped to the western capital,
translations.idiomatic: Without waiting for confirmation of the edict, Xu beheaded him as well and galloped to the western capital.

sentences.zh: 累遷左臺侍御史。

translations.literal: through successive promotions he became Attending Censor of the Left Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to Attending Censor of the Left Censorate.

sentences.zh: 時光祿少卿盧崇道以崔湜妻父，貶於嶺外。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Lu Chongdao, as father-in-law of Cui Shi, was demoted beyond the Lingnan frontier.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Lu Chongdao, as Cui Shi's father-in-law, was demoted beyond the Lingnan frontier.

sentences.zh: 逃歸，匿於東都，為仇家所發，詔旭究其獄。

translations.literal: He fled back and hid in the eastern capital; an enemy family reported him, and an edict ordered Xu to investigate his case.
translations.idiomatic: He fled back and hid in the eastern capital; an enemy family exposed him, and an edict ordered Xu to investigate the case.

sentences.zh: 旭欲擅其威權，因捕崇道親黨數十人，皆極其楚毒，然後結成其罪。

translations.literal: Xu wished to wield his authority arbitrarily; he therefore arrested several dozen of Chongdao's kin and associates, inflicted the utmost torture on all of them, and only then fixed their guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Xu wanted to wield arbitrary power; he arrested several dozen of Chongdao's kin and associates, tortured them to the limit, and only then fixed their guilt.

sentences.zh: 崇道及三子並杖死於都亭驛，門生親友皆決杖流貶。

translations.literal: Chongdao and his three sons were all beaten to death at the Capital Pavilion Post Station; his students, kin, and friends were all sentenced to beating and exile.
translations.idiomatic: Chongdao and his three sons were all beaten to death at the Capital Pavilion post station; his students, kin, and friends were all sentenced to beating and banishment.

sentences.zh: 時得罪多是知名之士，四海冤之。

translations.literal: At that time those convicted were mostly men of renown; the four seas considered it an injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Most of those convicted at the time were distinguished scholars, and the empire deemed it an outrage.

sentences.zh: 旭又與御史大夫李傑不葉，遞相糾訐，傑竟左遷衢州刺史。

translations.literal: Xu was again not on good terms with Grand Censor Li Jie; they mutually impeached each other, and Jie was ultimately demoted to Prefect of Qu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xu again clashed with Grand Censor Li Jie; they traded accusations until Jie was demoted to Prefect of Qu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 旭既得誌，擅行威福，由是朝廷畏而鄙之。

translations.literal: Once Xu had achieved his purpose, he wielded power and favor arbitrarily; from this the court both feared and despised him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xu had had his way, he wielded arbitrary power, and the court both feared and despised him.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷左司郎中，常帶侍御史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was transferred to Director of the Left Department and concurrently served as Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, he was promoted to Director of the Left Department, concurrently serving as Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 旭為吏嚴苛，左右無敢支梧，每銜命推劾，一見無不輸款者。

translations.literal: Xu was severe as an official; those around him dared not resist; whenever he carried orders to investigate, none who saw him failed to confess.
translations.idiomatic: As an official Xu was relentlessly harsh; none around him dared resist, and whenever he arrived on an investigative mission, every suspect confessed at once.

sentences.zh: 時宋王憲府掾紀希虬兄任劍南縣令，被告有贓私，旭使至蜀鞫之。

translations.literal: At that time the elder brother of Song Prince Xian's registrar Ji Xijiu served as Magistrate of Jiannan County; accused of graft, Xu sent men to Shu to interrogate him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the elder brother of Prince Xian's registrar Ji Xijiu served as magistrate of Jiannan County; accused of corruption, he was sent to Shu for interrogation on Xu's orders.

sentences.zh: 其妻美，旭威逼之，因奏決殺縣令，納贓數千萬。

translations.literal: His wife was beautiful; Xu coerced her, then memorialized that the magistrate be executed, and took bribes of tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was beautiful; Xu coerced her, then memorialized for the magistrate's execution and pocketed bribes worth tens of millions.

sentences.zh: 至六年，希虬遣奴詐為祗承人，受顧在臺，事旭累月。

translations.literal: By the sixth year, Xijiu sent a slave who feigned to be a messenger, was hired at the Censorate, and served Xu for many months.
translations.idiomatic: By the sixth year, Xijiu sent a slave who posed as a palace messenger, was hired at the Censorate, and served Xu for many months.

sentences.zh: 旭賞之，召入宅中，委以腹心。

translations.literal: Xu rewarded him, summoned him into his house, and entrusted him as a confidant.
translations.idiomatic: Xu rewarded him, summoned him into his home, and treated him as a trusted confidant.

sentences.zh: 其奴密記旭受饋遺囑托事，乃成數千貫，歸謁希虬。

translations.literal: The slave secretly recorded Xu's acceptance of gifts and commissions entrusted to him, amounting to several thousand strings of cash, then returned to pay respects to Xijiu.
translations.idiomatic: The slave secretly recorded Xu's bribes and favors, amounting to several thousand strings of cash, then returned to report to Xijiu.

sentences.zh: 希虬銜泣見憲，敘以家冤。

translations.literal: Xijiu, weeping inwardly, saw Prince Xian and recounted his family's grievance.
translations.idiomatic: Xijiu, choking back tears, went to Prince Xian and told him of his family's wrong.

sentences.zh: 憲憫之，執其狀以奏，詔付臺司劾之。

translations.literal: The prince took pity on him, submitted the written complaint, and an edict ordered the Censorate to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The prince took pity on him, submitted the written complaint, and an edict ordered the Censorate to investigate.

sentences.zh: 贓私累巨萬，貶龍平尉，憤恚而死，甚為時人之所慶快。

translations.literal: Graft totaling tens of thousands was found; he was demoted to Commandant of Longping; he died in rage and resentment, much to the joy of contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Graft totaling tens of thousands was proven; Xu was demoted to Commandant of Longping, where he died in fury—much to the relief of his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 吉溫吉溫，天官侍郎頊弟琚之孽子也。

translations.literal: Ji Wen—Ji Wen was the illegitimate son of Jun, younger brother of Vice Director of the Celestial Office Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Wen was the illegitimate son of Jun, younger brother of Vice Director Ji Shu of the Celestial Office.

sentences.zh: 譎詭能諂事人，遊於中貴門，愛若親戚。

translations.literal: Crafty and deceitful, skilled at flattery; he moved among eunuch circles and was treated like kin.
translations.idiomatic: Crafty and deceitful, a skilled flatterer, he moved among the eunuchs and was treated like one of the family.

sentences.zh: 性禁害，果於推劾。

translations.literal: By nature cruel and malicious, bold in investigation and impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: By nature cruel and malicious, he was ruthless in investigation and impeachment.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，為新豐丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianbao era, he served as Assistant Magistrate of Xinfeng.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianbao era, he served as assistant magistrate of Xinfeng.

sentences.zh: 時太子文學薛嶷承恩幸，引溫入對。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince's Literary Companion Xue Yi enjoyed imperial favor and brought Wen in for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the crown prince's literary companion Xue Yi enjoyed imperial favor and brought Wen in for an audience.

sentences.zh: 玄宗目之而謂嶷曰：「是一不良漢，朕不要也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong looked at him and said to Yi: "This is a bad fellow; I don't want him."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong looked him over and said to Yi: "This is a bad character—I want nothing to do with him."

sentences.zh: 時蕭炅為河南尹，河南府有事，京臺差溫推詰，事連炅，堅執不舍，賴炅與右相李林甫善，抑而免之。

translations.literal: At that time Xiao Jiong was Intendant of Henan; when Henan had a matter, the Capital Censorate assigned Wen to investigate; the case implicated Jiong; Wen persisted relentlessly, but thanks to Jiong's friendship with Right Chancellor Li Linfu, it was suppressed and he was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xiao Jiong was Intendant of Henan; when a case arose in Henan Prefecture, the Capital Censorate assigned Wen to investigate. The case implicated Jiong, and Wen pressed relentlessly—but Jiong's friendship with Right Chancellor Li Linfu got the matter suppressed and him cleared.

sentences.zh: 及溫選，炅已為京兆尹，一唱萬年尉，即就其官，人為危之。

translations.literal: When Wen was selected for appointment, Jiong was already Intendant of the Capital; at a single recommendation he became Commandant of Wannian, and immediately took up the post—people considered it perilous for him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen was selected for office, Jiong was already Intendant of the Capital; with a single recommendation Wen became commandant of Wannian and immediately took up the post—people thought him in grave peril.

sentences.zh: 時驃騎高力士常止宿宮禁，或時出外第，炅必謁焉。

translations.literal: At that time Cavalry General Gao Lishi often lodged within the palace; when he sometimes went to his outer residence, Jiong always called on him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Cavalry General Gao Lishi often stayed within the palace precincts; whenever he went to his outer residence, Jiong always paid his respects.

sentences.zh: 溫先馳與力士言謔甚洽，握手呼行第，炅覷之嘆伏。

translations.literal: Wen first rushed ahead to banter familiarly with Lishi, clasped hands and called him by familiar rank; Jiong watched and sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Wen rushed ahead to banter familiarly with Lishi, clasped his hand and called him by familiar rank; Jiong watched and sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 及他日，溫謁炅於府庭，遽布心腹曰：「他日不敢隳國家法，今日已後，洗心事公。」

translations.literal: On another day, Wen called on Jiong at his office and openly declared his loyalty: "In the past I dared not break the laws of the state; from today onward I devote myself wholly to you."
translations.idiomatic: On another day Wen called on Jiong at his office and openly pledged his loyalty: "In the past I dared not break the laws of the state; from today onward I devote myself wholly to you."

sentences.zh: 炅復與盡歡。

translations.literal: Jiong again feasted with him to the full.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong again feasted with him to the full.

sentences.zh: 會林甫與左相李適之、駙馬張垍不葉，適之兼兵部尚書，垍兄均為兵部侍郎，林甫遣人訐出兵部銓曹主簿事令史六十餘人偽濫事，圖覆其官長，詔出付京兆府與憲司對問。

translations.literal: When Lin Fuli was at odds with Left Chancellor Li Shizhi and Cavalry Commandant Zhang Ji, Shizhi concurrently served as Minister of War and Ji's elder brother Jun as Vice Minister of War, Lin Fuli sent someone to expose over sixty clerks of the War Ministry's selection office for fraudulent abuses, intending to overturn their superiors; an edict ordered the case handed to the Capital Intendancy and Censorate for joint inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Fuli was at odds with Left Chancellor Li Shizhi and Cavalry Commandant Zhang Ji; Shizhi concurrently served as Minister of War, and Ji's elder brother Jun as Vice Minister. Lin Fuli exposed over sixty clerks in the War Ministry's selection office for fraudulent abuses, intending to bring down their superiors. An edict ordered the case handed to the Capital Intendancy and Censorate for joint inquiry.

sentences.zh: 數日，竟不究其由。

translations.literal: After several days, they still had not traced the source of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: After several days they still had not traced the source of the affair.

sentences.zh: 炅使溫劾之。

translations.literal: Jiong had Wen investigate it.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong had Wen take over the investigation.

sentences.zh: 溫於院中分囚於兩處，溫於後廳佯取兩重囚訊之，或杖或壓，痛苦之聲，所不忍聞。

translations.literal: Wen divided prisoners in the courtyard into two places; in the rear hall he pretended to interrogate two heavy felons, beating or crushing them—the sounds of anguish were unbearable to hear.
translations.idiomatic: Wen divided the prisoners in the courtyard into two groups; in the rear hall he pretended to interrogate two hardened felons, beating or crushing them—the sounds of agony were unbearable.

sentences.zh: 即云：「若存性命，乞紙盡答。」

translations.literal: He then said: "If you wish to keep your lives, beg for paper and answer fully."
translations.idiomatic: He then said: "If you wish to keep your lives, beg for paper and answer in full."

sentences.zh: 令史輩素諳溫，各自誣伏罪，及溫引問，無敢違者。

translations.literal: The clerks had long known Wen's methods; each falsely confessed guilt, and when Wen summoned them for questioning, none dared disobey.
translations.idiomatic: The clerks had long known Wen's methods; each falsely confessed, and when Wen summoned them for questioning, none dared resist.

sentences.zh: 晷刻間事輯，驗囚無栲訊決罰處。

translations.literal: Within a short span the matter was concluded; when the prisoners were examined, there was no sign of interrogation or beating.
translations.idiomatic: Within a short span the matter was concluded; when the prisoners were examined, there was no sign of torture or beating.

sentences.zh: 常云：「若遇知己，南山白額獸不足縛也。」

translations.literal: He often said: "If I meet one who knows my worth, even the white-browed tiger of Mount Nan is not hard to bind."
translations.idiomatic: He often said: "If I meet one who knows my worth, even the white-browed tiger of Mount Nan is not hard to bind."

sentences.zh: 會李林甫將起刑獄，除不附己者，乃引之於門，與羅希奭同鍛煉詔獄。

translations.literal: When Li Linfu was about to launch criminal prosecutions to eliminate those not loyal to him, he brought Wen into his faction and had him work with Luo Xiyi to forge cases in the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Linfu was about to launch criminal prosecutions to eliminate those not loyal to him, he brought Wen into his circle and had him work with Luo Xiyi to forge cases in the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 五載，因中官納其外甥武敬一女為盛王琦妃，擢京兆府士曹。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianbao, through a eunuch he presented his niece, daughter of Wu Jing, as consort to Prince Sheng Qi; he was promoted to Records Officer of the Capital Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianbao, through a eunuch he presented his niece, Wu Jing's daughter, as consort to Prince Sheng Qi and was promoted to records officer of the Capital Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時林甫專謀不利於東儲，以左驍衛兵曹柳湜杜良娣妹婿，令溫推之。

translations.literal: At that time Lin Fuli devoted himself to schemes harmful to the Heir Apparent; since Left Valiant Guard Records Officer Liu Shi was son-in-law to Consort Du, Lin Fuli had Wen investigate him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Lin Fuli was scheming against the heir apparent; since Left Valiant Guard records officer Liu Shi was son-in-law to Consort Du, Lin Fuli had Wen investigate him.

sentences.zh: 溫追著作郎王曾、前右司禦率府倉曹王修己、左武衛司戈盧寧、左威衛騎曹徐徵同就臺鞫，數日而獄成。

translations.literal: Wen pursued Academician Wang Zeng, former Right Department Chief Steward Warehouse Officer Wang Xiuji, Left Martial Guard Arms Officer Lu Ning, and Left Martial Guard Cavalry Officer Xu Zheng, bringing them together to the Censorate for interrogation; within days the case was complete.
translations.idiomatic: Wen pursued Academician Wang Zeng, former Right Department chief steward warehouse officer Wang Xiuji, Left Martial Guard arms officer Lu Ning, and Left Martial Guard cavalry officer Xu Zheng, bringing them to the Censorate for joint interrogation; within days the case was complete.

sentences.zh: 勣等杖死，積屍於大理寺。

translations.literal: Shi and the others were beaten to death; corpses piled up in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Shi and the others were beaten to death, and corpses piled up in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 六載，林甫又以戶部侍郎、兼御史中丞楊慎矜違忤其旨，御史中丞王鉷與慎矜親而嫉之，同構其事，云：「蓄圖讖，以己是隋煬帝子孫，規於興復」，林甫又奏付溫鞫焉，慎矜下獄繫之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Lin Fuli again, because Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and Concurrent Vice Grand Censor Yang Shenjin had defied his intent, and Vice Grand Censor Wang Hong was kin to Shenjin yet jealous of him, jointly fabricated the case, saying: "He hoards prophecy charts, claiming himself a descendant of Emperor Yang of Sui and plotting restoration"; Lin Fuli again memorialized that Wen investigate; Shenjin was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, Lin Fuli again moved against Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and Concurrent Vice Grand Censor Yang Shenjin, who had defied him. Vice Grand Censor Wang Hong, though related to Shenjin, envied him and helped fabricate the charge: "Shenjin hoarded prophecy charts, claiming descent from Emperor Yang of Sui and plotting restoration." Lin Fuli memorialized that Wen investigate, and Shenjin was imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 使溫於東京收捕其兄少府少監慎餘、弟洛陽令慎名，於汝州捕其門客史敬忠。

translations.literal: He had Wen arrest in the eastern capital Shenjin's elder brother Vice Director of the Palace Workshop Shenyu and younger brother Luoyang Magistrate Shenming, and arrest his retainer Shi Jingzhong in Ru Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He had Wen arrest in the eastern capital Shenjin's elder brother Vice Director Shenyu of the Palace Workshop and younger brother Luoyang Magistrate Shenming, and arrest his retainer Shi Jingzhong in Ru Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 敬忠頗有學，嘗與朝貴遊。

translations.literal: Jingzhong was quite learned and had once associated with court nobles.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhong was quite learned and had once moved among court nobles.

sentences.zh: 蹉跎不進。

translations.literal: He drifted without advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He had drifted without advancement.

sentences.zh: 與溫父琚情契甚密，溫孩孺時，敬忠嘗抱撫之。

translations.literal: He was intimately close with Wen's father Jun; when Wen was a child, Jingzhong had once held and caressed him.
translations.idiomatic: He had been intimately close with Wen's father Jun; when Wen was a child, Jingzhong had once held and caressed him.

sentences.zh: 溫令河南丞姚開就擒之，鎖其頸，布袂蒙面以見溫。

translations.literal: Wen ordered Henan Assistant Magistrate Yao Kai to seize him, locked his neck, covered his face with cloth sleeves, and brought him before Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Wen ordered Henan assistant magistrate Yao Kai to seize him, locked a collar around his neck, covered his face with cloth sleeves, and brought him before Wen.

sentences.zh: 溫驅之於前，不交一言。

translations.literal: Wen drove him forward without exchanging a single word.
translations.idiomatic: Wen drove him forward without exchanging a single word.

sentences.zh: 欲及京，使典誘之云：「楊慎矜今款招己成，須子一辨。

translations.literal: Before reaching the capital, he had an attendant coax him, saying: "Yang Shenjin has already confessed; we need you to corroborate.
translations.idiomatic: Before reaching the capital, he had an attendant coax him, saying: "Yang Shenjin has already confessed; we need you to corroborate.

sentences.zh: 若解人意，必活；

translations.literal: If you understand what is wanted, you will certainly live;
translations.idiomatic: If you understand what is wanted, you will certainly live;

sentences.zh: 忤之，必死。」

translations.literal: if you resist, you will certainly die."
translations.idiomatic: if you resist, you will certainly die."

sentences.zh: 敬忠回首曰：「七郎，乞一紙。」

translations.literal: Jingzhong turned his head and said: "Seventh Brother, please give me a sheet of paper."
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhong turned his head and said: "Seventh Brother, please give me a sheet of paper."

sentences.zh: 溫佯不與，見詞懇，乃於桑下令答，三紙辯皆符溫旨。

translations.literal: Wen pretended to refuse; seeing his earnest plea, he had him answer under a mulberry tree; three sheets of testimony all matched Wen's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Wen pretended to refuse; seeing his earnest plea, he had him answer under a mulberry tree—three sheets of testimony, all matching Wen's intent.

sentences.zh: 喜曰：「丈人莫相怪！」

translations.literal: Delighted, he said: "Elder, don't hold it against me!"
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, he said: "Elder, don't hold it against me!"

sentences.zh: 遂徐下拜。

translations.literal: He then slowly prostrated himself.
translations.idiomatic: He then slowly prostrated himself.

sentences.zh: 及至溫湯，始鞫慎矜，以敬忠詞為證。

translations.literal: When they reached Wen Springs, Shenjin was interrogated for the first time, with Jingzhong's testimony as evidence.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Wen Springs, Shenjin was interrogated for the first time, with Jingzhong's testimony as evidence.

sentences.zh: 及再搜其家，不得圖讖。

translations.literal: When they searched his home again, no prophecy charts were found.
translations.idiomatic: When they searched his home again, no prophecy charts were found.

sentences.zh: 林甫恐事泄，危之，乃使御史盧鉉入搜。

translations.literal: Lin Fuli feared the affair would leak and put him at risk, so he had Investigator Lu Xuan conduct the search.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Fuli feared the affair would leak and endanger him, so he had investigator Lu Xuan conduct the search.

sentences.zh: 鉉乃袖讖書而入，於隱僻中詬而出曰：「逆賊牢藏秘記，今得之矣！」

translations.literal: Xuan concealed the prophecy book in his sleeve, entered, then cursed aloud from a hidden spot: "The traitor had secret writings locked away—now we have them!"
translations.idiomatic: Xuan concealed the prophecy book in his sleeve, entered, then cursed aloud from a hidden spot: "The traitor had secret writings locked away—now we have them!"

sentences.zh: 指於慎矜小妻韓珠團婢，見舉家惶懼，且行捶擊，誰敢忤焉！

translations.literal: He pointed at Shenjin's young wife and maid Han Zhutuan; seeing the whole household in terror, they beat them as they went—who dared resist!
translations.idiomatic: He pointed at Shenjin's young wife and maid Han Zhutuan; seeing the whole household in terror, they beat them as they went—who dared resist!

sentences.zh: 獄乃成，慎矜兄弟賜死。

translations.literal: The case was complete; the Shenjin brothers were ordered to take their own lives.
translations.idiomatic: The case was complete, and the Shenjin brothers were ordered to take their own lives.

sentences.zh: 溫自是威振，衣冠不敢偶言。

translations.literal: From then on Wen's power was terrifying; officials dared not even speak casually.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Wen's power was terrifying, and officials dared not even speak casually.

sentences.zh: 溫早以嚴毒聞，頻知詔獄，忍行枉濫，推事未訊問，已作奏狀，計贓數。

translations.literal: Wen had long been known for severity and cruelty; he frequently handled imperial prison cases, ruthlessly committing injustice—even before interrogation he would draft memorials and calculate embezzlement figures.
translations.idiomatic: Wen had long been known for severity and cruelty; he frequently handled imperial prison cases and ruthlessly committed injustice—even before interrogation he would draft memorials and calculate embezzlement figures.

sentences.zh: 及被引問，便懾懼，即隨意而書，無敢惜其生者。

translations.literal: When brought for questioning, prisoners were frightened and wrote whatever was demanded, not daring to cling to their lives.
translations.idiomatic: When brought for questioning, prisoners were terrified and wrote whatever was demanded, not daring to cling to their lives.

sentences.zh: 因不加栲擊，獄成矣。

translations.literal: Thus without applying torture, the case was complete.
translations.idiomatic: Thus without applying torture, the case was complete.

sentences.zh: 林甫深以溫為能，擢戶部郎中，常帶御史。

translations.literal: Lin Fuli deeply regarded Wen as capable; he was promoted to Director of the Ministry of Revenue, concurrently serving as Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Fuli deeply regarded Wen as capable and promoted him to Director of the Ministry of Revenue, concurrently serving as Censor.

sentences.zh: 林甫雖倚以爪牙，溫又見安祿山受主恩，驃騎高力士居中用事，皆附會其間，結為兄弟。

translations.literal: Though Lin Fuli relied on him as a henchman, Wen also saw that An Lushan enjoyed the emperor's favor and Cavalry General Gao Lishi held power at court; he attached himself to them all and sealed brotherhood with them.
translations.idiomatic: Though Lin Fuli relied on him as a henchman, Wen also saw that An Lushan enjoyed the emperor's favor and Cavalry General Gao Lishi held power at court; he attached himself to them all and swore brotherhood with them.

sentences.zh: 常謂祿山曰：「李右相雖觀察人事，親於三兄，必不以兄為宰相。

translations.literal: He often told Lushan: "Right Chancellor Li may watch affairs closely and be close to you, Third Brother, but he will never make you chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: He often told Lushan: "Right Chancellor Li may watch affairs closely and be close to you, Third Brother, but he will never make you chancellor.

sentences.zh: 溫雖被驅使，必不超擢。

translations.literal: And though I am put to use, I will certainly not be promoted beyond my station.
translations.idiomatic: And though I am put to use, I will certainly not be promoted beyond my station.

sentences.zh: 若三兄奏溫為相，即奏兄堪大任，擠出林甫，是兩人必為相矣。」

translations.literal: If Third Brother memorializes that I be made chancellor, I will memorialize that you are fit for great responsibility and drive out Lin Fuli—then both of us will surely become chancellors."
translations.idiomatic: If Third Brother memorializes that I be made chancellor, I will memorialize that you are fit for great responsibility and drive out Lin Fuli—then both of us will surely become chancellors."

sentences.zh: 祿山悅之。

translations.literal: Lushan was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan was pleased.

sentences.zh: 時祿山承恩無敵，驟言溫能，玄宗亦忘曩歲之語。

translations.literal: At that time Lushan's imperial favor was unmatched; he suddenly praised Wen's abilities, and Emperor Xuanzong also forgot what he had said years before.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Lushan's imperial favor was unmatched; he suddenly praised Wen's abilities, and Emperor Xuanzong forgot what he had said years before.

sentences.zh: 十載，祿山加河東節度，因奏溫為河東節度副使，並知節度營田及管內采訪監察留後事。
